stories.headline: Uddhav Thackeray backs youth agitation over voter deletions, slams police crackdown at Dussehra rally
stories.deck: Thackeray warned that the government was underestimating the anger of the younger generation, arguing that their grievances reflected years of accumulated frustration over economic hardship and government policies
stories.bodyText:
Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) threw his weight behind the ongoing youth-led protests against alleged electoral irregularities, accusing the BJP-led government of suppressing dissent through police action and warning that continued disregard for the younger generation’s grievances could lead to widespread unrest.
Addressing the party’s annual Dussehra rally at Shivaji Park in Dadar, Mr. Thackeray criticised the police action against protesters in Delhi, questioned the labelling of demonstrators as “urban Naxals” and called for a change of government.
The remarks came amid demonstrations led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the deletion of names from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The agitation intensified following the detention of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka and restrictions on the October 16 ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ demonstration in Delhi.
Questioning RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s remarks on maintaining civility during protests, Mr. Thackeray accused the police of mistreating young demonstrators.
“Mr. Bhagwat says there should be civility during protests. But who should maintain civility? When young people are beaten, their clothes are torn, and they are treated like animals, where is the civility?” he asked.
Recalling his visit to protesters at Jantar Mantar following an alleged police crackdown, Mr. Thackeray said he had met several injured demonstrators, including women.
He claimed that some protesters had suffered head injuries, while others had fractured limbs or injuries from being assaulted. He also referred to a woman protester who alleged that her clothes had been torn during the police action.
Mr. Thackeray further cited accounts of protesters who had subsequently met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and alleged that they had been punched and kicked by police personnel.
Questioning why young people were being treated as criminals for demanding their rights, he said, “Nobody has a hobby of coming onto the streets, getting beaten by police, returning home and then facing police action again. They are coming out because they want justice.”
He warned that the government was underestimating the anger of the younger generation, arguing that their grievances reflected years of accumulated frustration over economic hardship and government policies.
Referring to people he met during the agitation, Mr. Thackeray recounted speaking to a man who claimed to have lost his livelihood following demonetisation. He accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah of pushing citizens into financial hardship over the past 12 years.
Drawing parallels with India’s freedom struggle, Mr. Thackeray invoked revolutionaries including Khudiram Bose, Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad, arguing that young people had historically played a decisive role in movements against injustice.
He also referred to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s achievements at a young age and questioned why the government was dismissing the concerns of today’s youth.
“Those who do not rise against injustice should not take Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s name,” he said.
Mr. Thackeray also questioned the Maharashtra government’s submissions before the Bombay High Court, describing the State as a centre of urban Naxalism.
“Which city in Maharashtra has become a centre of urban Naxalism? Why are these children coming onto the streets?” he asked, accusing the authorities of branding protesters as criminals rather than addressing their demands.
Turning to the electoral roll controversy, Mr. Thackeray questioned the deletion of nearly 13 crore names during the SIR exercise, comparing the figure with Maharashtra’s entire population.
“Are you saying all these 13 crore people are Bangladeshis?” he asked.
The nationwide revision exercise removed more than 13 crore names from draft electoral rolls. The Election Commission of India has said the exercise aims to remove ineligible or duplicate entries while protecting eligible voters’ rights, and has ordered a special enrolment drive for those left out.
Mr. Thackeray also criticised restrictions on protesters carrying the national flag and questioned the RSS’s history of hoisting the tricolour at its Nagpur headquarters.
Warning police personnel against using excessive force, he reminded them that their families were part of the same society as the protesters and urged them to consider the consequences of their actions.
On other issues, Mr. Thackeray criticised the State government’s handling of farmers’ distress, questioned the adequacy of the recently announced ₹5,000 assistance and raised concerns over law and order following the firing incident targeting Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff.
He urged Shiv Sena workers to resist injustice and work towards a change of government, reiterating his ambition to see the saffron flag flying not only over the Maharashtra legislature but also at the Red Fort in Delhi.

stories.headline: Oil prices today: Brent crude tops $110 as Middle East tensions threaten shipments
stories.deck: Oil prices have risen due to growing concerns over disruptions in Middle East supplies and threats to shipping routes. Recent attacks on vessels and infrastructure have heightened worries among traders and analysts. While Brent crude futures climbed to $110.10, WTI crude also saw an increase following previous declines. US officials are working with refiners to address rising fuel prices and…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices rose on Wednesday as traders weighed concerns over Middle East supplies amid growing risks to shipping in the Red Sea and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
Brent crude futures climbed $1.34, or 1.23 per cent, to $110.10 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $1.18, or 1.21 per cent, to $99 per barrel.
The gains followed a decline in the previous session, when prices eased after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts with Pakistan's army chief during a meeting in Tehran.
Tanker attacks raise concerns over oil supplies
Supply concerns intensified after a supertanker caught fire after striking a sea mine south of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy.
Iranian media reported that the vessel had been “violating” Iranian regulations.
At least 18 vessel attacks were reported over a two-week period, ship-tracking firm Kpler said in a note on Monday.
The attacks have also spread beyond the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil shipments.
“Attacks on tankers have expanded beyond the Strait of Hormuz,” LSEG analysts said in a note.
“Iran has been targeting vessels as far south as the Gulf of Oman, threatening loadings outside of the Arab Gulf, as well as the ship-to-ship transfers that have helped to support Middle East loadings as the conflict has dragged on,” the analysts added.
The Houthis on Monday claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and the airports in Riyadh and Abha, Saudi Arabia.
Meanwhile, the death toll from a Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces on Monday rose to 73 as fighting intensified, Reuters reported.
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said in a television interview aired on Tuesday that Tehran had not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks.
Oil prices retreat from five-month high
Despite Wednesday's gains, crude prices had fallen in the previous session after reaching elevated levels.
Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69 per cent, at $108.79 per barrel on Tuesday, after touching a five-month high of $111.99.
The November contract for US WTI crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled $1.87 lower, down 1.8 per cent, at $101.79 per barrel.
US works to increase fuel supplies
In the United States, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday that they were working with refiners around the world to increase fuel production as a diesel shortage pushed prices higher.
US crude oil inventories were also expected to have declined in the week ended October 16, alongside stocks of refined petroleum products, according to an extended Reuters poll.
The eight analysts surveyed by Reuters estimated that US crude inventories fell by an average of around 800,000 barrels during the week.
Market participants are monitoring developments across the Middle East, including threats to shipping routes and energy infrastructure, for their potential impact on oil supplies and prices.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu rain: Schools in Chennai, four other districts declare holiday
stories.deck: The weather stations in Meenambakkam and Nungambakkam recorded 12 cm and 11 cm of rainfall respectively, followed by Taramani (10 cm) Madhavaram (9 cm), Villivakkam and Nandanam (8 cm)
stories.bodyText:
Schools in five districts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, will remain closed on Wednesday (October 21, 2026), owing to heavy rain, according to district authorities.
The Collectors of Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, and Chengalpattu districts have declared a holiday for schools, while a similar order has been issued in Ranipet district due to rain.
Several places in and around Chennai received heavy rainfall till 6 a.m. on Wednesday (October 21), according to Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) data. The weather stations in Meenambakkam and Nungambakkam recorded 12 cm and 11 cm of rainfall respectively, followed by Taramani (10 cm) Madhavaram (9 cm), Villivakkam and Nandanam (8 cm). Various other districts, including Coimbatore, Kancheepuram, Ramanathapuram Thoothukudi and Kanniyakumari, also received rainfall.
Light to moderate rainfall is likely to continue at isolated places across several parts of the State until 10 a.m. on Wednesday (October 21), according to the latest weather update.
The districts likely to receive rainfall include Chennai, Tiruvallur, Ranipet, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Mayiladuthurai, Nagapattinam, Tiruvarur, Thanjavur, Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli, and Kanniyakumari.
A fresh system, over the Bay of Bengal, is likely to sustain intense rainfall across Tamil Nadu till October 26, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) said.
It issued orange alerts for a few southern districts, including Tirunelveli and Thoothukudi, as they may receive heavy to very heavy rainfall up to 20 cm on Wednesday (October 21) and Thursday (October 22).

stories.headline: Woman claims Rs 14.7L home relief; taxman cites multiple homes, why ITAT gave relief
stories.deck: The Income Tax Department reopened a woman’s assessment for assessment year 2015-16, alleging that she had wrongly claimed a Rs 14.70 lakh deduction under Section 54F of the Income Tax Act. The Assessing Officer denied the deduction on the ground that she owned more than one residential house apart from the new asset, and assessed her income at Rs 16,70,500.
stories.bodyText:
You own a house and claim exemption under Section 54F of the Income Tax Act. However, the exemption is denied because the Income Tax Department believes you own more than one property.
In one such case, the dispute arose because the income tax department considered that the woman owned more than one house property, making her ineligible for the deduction.
However, in its order pronounced on September 10, 2026, the tribunal allowed her appeal and reversed the decision of the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals).
Also Read | 
Cook working in a 5-star hotel gets Rs 4 crore tax notice with penalty for alleged Rs 24.62 crore sales, but he claims PAN was misused which led to wrong Form 26AS entry; why Delhi HC gave relief
What the case is about
The Income Tax Department reopened a woman’s assessment for assessment year 2015-16, alleging that she had wrongly claimed a Rs 14.70 lakh deduction under Section 54F of the Income Tax Act.
The Assessing Officer denied the deduction on the ground that she owned more than one residential house apart from the new asset, and assessed her income at Rs 16,70,500.
The woman challenged the assessment before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), National Faceless Appeal Centre, but her appeal was dismissed on August 20, 2025.
The assessment proceedings referred to three properties in Nagpur. The question before the tribunal was whether the ownership of the other properties meant she failed to meet the conditions for claiming the benefit.
The tribunal described the dispute as follows: “The sole grievance of the assessee is against the deduction u/s.54F of the Act by the Revenue authorities alleging that assessee owned more than one house property making the assessee disentitled for claiming deduction u/s.54F of the Act.”
Also Read | 
Husband and wife sell property; Income Tax dept alleges Rs 3.30 crore sale against Rs 1.60 crore in deed, cites WhatsApp chats, Excel sheets to claim Rs 1.70 crore cash receipts, but ITAT gives relief
Why did ITAT rule in favour of the home owner?
The tribunal examined three properties mentioned in the assessment proceedings and found that one belonged to a company in which the woman was a director, while another was jointly owned by her and her husband.
It held that the company's property could not be treated as her personally owned property merely because of her association with the company.
The flat was jointly owned by the woman and her husband, although she had not contributed towards its purchase.
The order records: “So far as the third property, the same is jointly owned by the assessee and her husband and the assessee has not provided any amount towards the purchase of the said property.”
The tribunal concluded that the woman fulfilled the conditions for claiming the deduction, stating: “The assessee has fulfilled the necessary conditions for claiming deduction u/s.54F of the Act and therefore entitled to deduction u/s.54F of the Act at Rs 14,70,000/-.”
Also Read | 
Woman applied for 130 IPO shares, bank entered only 65; consumer commission awards Rs 37,000 for deficient service but rejects her Rs 40 lakh compensation claim
The order identifies one house property owned by the woman for the purpose of its conclusion.
The tribunal reversed the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals)’s finding, stating: “Finding of ld.CIT(A) is reversed.” It allowed the woman’s grounds of appeal and concluded: “In the result, the appeal of the assessee is allowed.”
The tribunal thus granted the Rs 14.70 lakh deduction after examining the specific property-ownership facts before it.
Kuldip Kumar, Partner at Mainstay Tax Advisors LLP notes that owning more than one residential house is one of the most common grounds on which tax authorities deny exemption under Section 54F of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
In this case, the tax authorities considered three properties while denying the exemption. The ITAT observed that one property was owned by a company in which the taxpayer was a director and, therefore, could not be treated as her property merely because of her directorship.
The second property was the new house acquired for claiming the Section 54F exemption and was consequently excluded from the count.
The third property was jointly owned by the taxpayer and her husband. Although the taxpayer had not contributed towards its purchase, the Tribunal treated her as a joint owner of that property.
The Tribunal concluded that the taxpayer owned only one residential house other than the new asset and, therefore, fulfilled the relevant ownership condition for claiming the exemption under Section 54F.
“There have been several favourable judicial decisions in which appellate authorities have held that fractional or joint ownership of residential properties should not necessarily be equated with exclusive ownership for determining eligibility under Section 54F,” he tells TOI.
In some cases, taxpayers have been allowed to claim the exemption despite holding fractional interests in multiple residential properties.
Also Read | 
He inherited land from mother, redeveloped home & received Rs 75 lakh from builder; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT Delhi gives relief, ruling multiple floors can qualify as one house
Significance of ruling
According to Kuldip Kumar, this ITAT ruling highlights the importance of examining the facts and ownership of each property before determining eligibility for the exemption.
“Joint ownership of residential property, particularly between spouses, is common. It may arise from inheritance, estate planning, the desire to avoid future family disputes or the need to ensure that the surviving spouse can manage the property without unnecessary complications,” he adds.
“For taxpayers claiming exemption under Section 86 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (corresponding to Section 54F of the Income-tax Act, 1961), these favourable judicial precedents may provide support where jointly owned properties are involved. However, the outcome will depend on the facts of each case and the judicial precedents applicable to it, and the possibility of the tax authorities taking a contrary view cannot be ruled out,” Kumar tells TOI.
“A legislative clarification specifying how jointly owned or fractional interests in residential properties should be counted for the purposes of this provision would provide greater certainty, reduce litigation and benefit taxpayers at large,” he adds.

briefs.headline: J&K government announces annual shifting of capital from Srinagar to Jammu
briefs.deck: According to the ‘Darbar Move’ calendar, the offices are scheduled to reopen in the winter capital of Jammu on November 2. In summer capital Srinagar, offices will start closing from October 30 and October 31
briefs.bodyText:
The J&K government on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) announced the annual shifting of capital from Srinagar to Jammu, a practice stopped by the Lieutenant Governor’s administration after 2021 and resumed by the Omar Abdullah government in 2025.
To ferry employees and official files, the government directed the Jammu and Kashmir Road Transport Corporation (JKRTC) “to arrange an adequate number of buses in good condition to transport employees on October 31 and November 1.”
“Tickets will be issued in advance from October 27,” said a government spokesman.
The government directed the JKRTC that each convoy of buses be accompanied by a crane, two empty buses and mobile workshops to deal with any eventuality during the journey.
“The Jammu and Kashmir Police will provide security to the convoys and ensure their precedence at the Banihal-Qazigund Tunnel and the Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel,” the order said.
According to the ‘Darbar Move’ calendar, the offices are scheduled to reopen in the winter capital of Jammu on November 2. In summer capital Srinagar, offices will start closing from October 30 and October 31.
“Offices moving in camp mode will carry up to 33 per cent of their staff strength or 10 officials, whichever is lower, unless specified otherwise,” the order said.
Introduced in 1872 by Dogra Maharaja Gulab Singh, the ‘Darbar Move’ allowed shifting of offices from Jammu to Srinagar when summers peaked there and return to Jammu as winter peaked in the Valley.
The practice was stopped by the Lieutenant Governor’s administration in 2021, on account of burden on the exchequer. However, J&K’s regional parties, including the ruling National Conference (NC), was in favour of the practice, which also acts as a bridge between two diverse cultures of Kashmir and Jammu.
More than 9000 government employees would relocate every year from around 51 government departments to the twin capitals as part of the practice.

briefs.headline: Dussehra 2026: Traffic curbs in Dwarka, security tightened in Delhi-NCR and more
briefs.deck: As per the Delhi Traffic Police advisory, restrictions may be imposed on six roads in Dwarka on October 20 evening
briefs.bodyText:
In view of the Dussehra celebrations, security has been tightened around Delhi-NCR area, while the traffic police have issued advisory on the roads that are likely to be affected on Tuesday (October 20, 2026).
Traffic restrictions may be imposed in Dwarka and parts of South Delhi, the police have said.

Traffic curbs in Dwarka
The Delhi Traffic Police have issued an advisory, pointing out that restrictions may be imposed on six roads in Dwarka on Tuesday (October 20) evening. This is in view of the heavy pedestrian and vehicular movement expected due to a large gathering and anticipated VVIP movement.

Dussehra celebrations at Red Fort
In view of the Dussehra celebrations at Red Fort, the Delhi Traffic Police have said that traffic restrictions and parking regulations will be imposed from 3 p.m. to 11 p.m. on October 20. As per the advisory, traffic movement on Netaji Subhash Marg and Nishad Raj Marg may be restricted or regulated depending on prevailing traffic conditions and security requirements.

As per a PTI report, around 2,200 police personnel have been deployed at 66 ‘Ravan Dahan’ sites, 17 religious processions and other related events in Gurugram. Elaborate security arrangements with 1,200 police personnel have also been made in Faridabad to maintain law and order.

briefs.headline: Tiger Shroff firing case: Four arrested for allegedly transporting firearm to Mumbai, helping coordinate operation
briefs.deck: The Special Cell’s statement does not establish whether the pistol allegedly transported by the accused has been conclusively linked to the firing incident or whether the alleged attempt to arrange the shooters’ escape was successful
briefs.bodyText:
The Delhi Police Special Cell on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) arrested four people, including two women, for their alleged role in transporting a firearm to Mumbai ahead of the October 18 firing incident targeting Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff’s car. According to the police, the accused were acting on the instructions of Anil Pandit, who allegedly coordinated their movements through an encrypted messaging application.
The accused have been identified as Kunal, 21, and Sumit, 19, both residents of Sonipat in Haryana, and Radha, 23, and Babita, 23, residents of Sitapur and Azamgarh districts in Uttar Pradesh, respectively.
According to a statement issued by the Special Cell, Kunal, who had recently been released on bail, was introduced to Pandit through a friend from Harsana village in Haryana. The two subsequently began communicating through an encrypted messaging application.
The police alleged that Kunal travelled to Amritsar on Pandit’s instructions to collect a pistol and 20 rounds of ammunition. Sumit allegedly accompanied him on the trip.
Investigators said Kunal had met Radha about two months earlier and developed a relationship with her. He allegedly disclosed details of his activities to her and persuaded her to travel to Mumbai with the firearm.
On October 15, Kunal allegedly accompanied Radha and Babita to New Delhi Railway Station, from where the two women boarded a train to Mumbai. The pistol was concealed in Radha’s bag, the police said. Kunal allegedly remained in contact with Pandit through the encrypted application and relayed his instructions to the women during their journey.
The two women reached Dadar on October 17 and checked into a hotel. At around 11 a.m. that day, a minor boy allegedly collected the bag containing the firearm from Radha near the hotel, according to the Special Cell.
The following day, at around 7 p.m., shots were fired at Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai. After the incident, Pandit allegedly contacted Kunal and told him that the shooters were stranded in Mumbai. He then instructed Kunal to arrange their escape, the police alleged.
Meanwhile, Radha and Babita left Mumbai on the Dadar-Haridwar Express on October 18.
The Special Cell said the two women were apprehended at New Delhi Railway Station on Tuesday (October 20), while Kunal and Sumit were apprehended in Sonipat.
All four were subsequently arrested and produced before a court under Section 35(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
Officials from the Maharashtra Police’s Crime Investigation Department (CID), Mumbai, subsequently moved an application before the court seeking permission to interrogate the accused in custody and formally arrest them in connection with the firing case. The court allowed the application, following which the Maharashtra Police team formally arrested all four accused.
The court also granted a subsequent application seeking three days’ transit remand, allowing the investigators to take the accused to Mumbai for further investigation.
The arrests point to a suspected operation involving the procurement and transportation of a firearm across State borders. However, the Special Cell’s statement does not establish whether the pistol allegedly transported by the accused has been conclusively linked to the firing incident or whether the alleged attempt to arrange the shooters’ escape was successful.

briefs.headline: Rubio says India-U.S. trade deal close, urges New Delhi to boost U.S. energy, defence buys
briefs.deck: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said both sides welcomed the progress made in negotiations on the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement and reaffirmed their commitment to working towards its early conclusion
briefs.bodyText:
India and the U.S. moved to expand energy and defence cooperation on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) despite ongoing friction in their relations, as Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged New Delhi to scale up energy trade and increase purchases of American technologies and systems.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar hosted Mr. Rubio for wide-ranging talks shortly after the top diplomat arrived in Mumbai for his second visit to India in under five months, even as bilateral ties remain strained over Washington's unpredictable trade policies and tightening immigration rules.
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said both sides welcomed the progress made in negotiations on the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement and reaffirmed their commitment to working towards its early conclusion.
Ahead of his meeting with Mr. Jaishankar, Mr. Rubio described India as a crude oil refining "superpower" and advocated for processing more Venezuelan crude in India. The Secretary of State is scheduled to visit Reliance Industries Ltd.-owned Jamnagar Refinery on Wednesday (October 21, 2026).
Mr. Rubio, answering a question on the trade pact during a brief media interaction ahead of the meeting, said that "a small number of items are left to be wrapped up" and hoped it will be sealed "shortly".
"I would say we're about as close as you can be without having an executed agreement. I think there's a small number of items left to wrap up. So I think that will happen shortly — we're hoping, which it should — and hopefully have some good news to announce fairly soon. And perhaps the leaders can sign it thereafter," he said.
Following the meeting, Mr. Jaishankar said on social media that he and Mr. Rubio "shared views on further advancement of our ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties."
The U.S. State Department said the Secretary and the External Affairs Minister discussed regional and global issues, including developments in West Asia.
"The Secretary reiterated that increased energy trade with the United States can play a transformative role in diversifying India's supply chains while meeting its sizeable consumer demand," it said.
"He also commended recent progress in bilateral defence and civil nuclear cooperation, and advocated for the increased purchase of U.S. technologies and systems, which can enhance the security and prosperity of both our countries," the State Department added.
In a late evening statement, the MEA said the two sides reviewed the entire gamut of India-U.S. relations and discussed ways to further strengthen the Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.
"Both sides had a detailed exchange of views on a wide range of areas, including trade, defence, technology and energy security. They also exchanged views on regional and global developments," it said.
The MEA said Mr. Rubio's visit reflected the sustained momentum of high-level exchanges between the two countries, underscoring the importance both sides attach to further advancing the India-U.S. ties for the 21st century.
Before his talks with Mr. Jaishankar, Mr. Rubio visited the Taj memorial and laid a wreath in honour of the victims of the horrific 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks that included six American citizens.
"In Mumbai, Indian External Affairs Minister @DrSJaishankar and I discussed energy security and defence cooperation while reaffirming the importance of advancing the U.S.-India strategic partnership," Mr. Rubio said on X.
U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said Mr. Rubio and Mr. Jaishankar had "productive discussions" on deepening U.S.-India cooperation across defence, energy, emerging technologies, and trade, as "we continue to build the unrivalled momentum in our bilateral partnership." The envoy was also present at the meeting.
In his brief media interaction, Mr. Rubio also responded to a question on whether the U.S. administration was upset with New Delhi over the amount of Russian oil it procured last year and its efforts to reduce the volume.
"I think what India has expressed repeatedly is its desire to diversify its energy portfolio, which is a smart thing to do. Obviously, it's not easy to do that from one day to the next day," he said.
"I think they've made substantial progress in that regard, and we're happy to see that. But in the end, it's not just about Russian oil; it's about their desire to diversify, and obviously we think we can be a source of some of their energy inputs," he said.
"Obviously, we've discussed Venezuela and other countries, and I think it's in our interest to have a strong ally with a diverse energy portfolio," he added.
The U.S. Secretary of State also hailed India's oil refining capabilities.
"India is a refining superpower. They have the ability to do that, and they have companies that know how to do that," Mr. Rubio said, pointing out that certain Indian companies have "pre-existing oil concessions in Venezuela".
"I'm not claiming to you that Venezuela alone can fill the hole that could be caused by some of the things that are happening around the world, but I think over time, it most certainly can, and in the short term, it can certainly provide the means," he said.
"So, that's one of the things we'll talk about. With India, we've talked about it in the past, and they sound ready. They're ready to do it, they're willing to do it," he noted.
The top diplomat also answered a question on his trip to Reliance Industries Ltd.'s refinery in Jamnagar on Wednesday (October 20, 2026).
"Energy is related to national security. Countries fight wars over energy; economies collapse over lack of energy. We're going to go see a company that has a tremendous amount of refining capability. It makes all the sense in the world to talk to them about it," he said.
During the media interaction, Mr. Rubio said several geopolitical developments — including the situation in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks on energy pipelines in Saudi Arabia — impacted energy supplies, causing several countries to grapple with a diesel shortage.
Last week, U.S. President Donald Trump suspended certain sanctions against Russia and five of the biggest buyers of Russian oil, including India. He also announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release hundreds of thousands of tonnes of Russian diesel onto the world market.
"We must continue our strong partnership in combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations," Mr. Jaishankar said in a social media post.
"At the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, I laid a wreath honouring the victims of the horrific November 26, 2008 terrorist attacks, including six American citizens," Mr. Rubio said.
"We remember those lost, honour the courage of those who responded, and reaffirm the enduring U.S.-India partnership and our shared commitment to combating terrorism," he added.
Mr. Jaishankar, addressing a reception celebrating 250 Years of American Independence, said Indian talent and Indian skills have helped "shape the tech era in the U.S."
"Of course, we've had our share of issues, including the manner in which we approach the world and its challenges. But in the last few decades, our partnership has steadily expanded, acquiring new dimensions and new facets," he said.

briefs.headline: Dale Steyn’s 18-year-old record falls as Harmer scripts history against Australia
briefs.deck: Simon Harmer made headlines with an impressive 82 in the second Test against Australia, eclipsing the previous record of 76 runs held by Dale Steyn for South African No. 9 batsmen. His performance was vital in rescuing South Africa from a challenging position of 110-6. Partnering with Temba Bavuma, their formidable eighth-wicket alliance totaled 183 runs. South Africa eventually declared at…
briefs.bodyText:
Simon Harmer
 etched his name in South African cricket history with a career-best effort against Australia, breaking Dale Steyn’s record for the highest individual score by a South African No. 9 or lower against the visitors.
Harmer scored 82 in South Africa’s first innings on Day 3 of the second Test at St George’s Park in Gqeberha on Tuesday, surpassing Steyn’s previous record of 76, made in Melbourne in 2008.
The off-spinner struck 10 fours and a six in his 91-ball innings, providing crucial support to skipper 
Temba Bavuma
 as South Africa recovered from 110-6 to declare at 425-9.
Harmer’s maiden Test half-century came at a pivotal stage after Australia had put the hosts under pressure. Bavuma and Marco Jansen had already combined for a 132-run stand for the seventh wicket before Jansen fell for 85.
Harmer then joined Bavuma to add 183 runs for the eighth wicket, putting South Africa firmly back in control. It was the second-highest partnership for the eighth wicket or lower in South African Test history, behind Mark Boucher and Pat Symcox’s 195-run stand against Pakistan in Johannesburg in 1998.
The partnership also moved past the 180-run stand between JP Duminy and Steyn against Australia in Melbourne in 2008, underlining the significance of Harmer’s contribution.
Bavuma made 179, his highest Test score, after facing 334 deliveries and hitting 18 fours and a six. He had walked in with South Africa at 12-2 on the opening day and held the innings together through multiple batting collapses.
Harmer’s innings ended when he was bowled by Marnus Labuschagne, leaving him short of a maiden Test century. South Africa declared soon after Bavuma was dismissed by Mitchell Starc.
Australia were 3-1 at stumps after 
Kagiso Rabada
 dismissed Nic Maddinson for a four-ball duck late in the day.
Australia won the first Test in Durban by 214 runs and lead the three-match series 1-0.

briefs.headline: Musk ordered Starlink slowdown, kept Ukraine and Trump administration in dark
briefs.deck: US officials, however, have denied ordering any slowdown. Defence secretary Pete Hegseth said Washington had not directed any reduction in the satellite services, while secretary of state Marco Rubio maintained that the White House was not responsible for the reported disruption. Speaking to reporters, Hegseth said the US military had not instructed any changes to the satellite service used by…
briefs.bodyText:
Elon Musk’s 
SpaceX
 has come under scrutiny over reported disruptions to satellite internet services used by Ukrainian forces, with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accusing the company of restricting access during the war with Russia.
A report by The Wall Street Journal, citing officials familiar with the matter, said Musk had directed an intentional slowdown of Ukraine’s essential military Starlink network, triggering alarm in Kyiv and leaving the Trump administration bewildered.
US officials, however, have denied ordering any slowdown. Defence secretary Pete Hegseth said Washington had not directed any reduction in the satellite services, while secretary of state Marco Rubio maintained that the White House was not responsible for the reported disruption.
US says it did not order a slowdown
Speaking to reporters, Hegseth said the US military had not instructed any changes to the satellite service used by Ukraine.
"We haven't pulled anything back," Hegseth said. "Nothing's changed from our view. We haven't made any directives or anything like that. And we wish the Ukrainians obviously success."
He said any operational changes or performance adjustments would fall under the satellite provider's contractual terms.
"There are terms of service that ultimately need to be complied with," Hegseth added, noting that "that's where Starlink has the option to make those decisions."
Rubio also rejected claims that Washington had ordered Starlink's speed to be reduced. He stressed that Starlink is a commercial service operated by SpaceX, whereas Starshield is a separate military-grade system controlled by the US government.
"Starshield is a defence and military product; that is something that the United States military uses. It is not available to Ukraine, and it is under discussion how they want to use it. I don’t know if Zelenskyy knows what he is talking about. In the United States, nobody ordered that Starlink's speed be slowed down. In my understanding, it has been restored. That is Starlink; they were using Starlink. Starshield is in contract with the US military, has nothing to do with Ukraine."
Rubio said Ukraine was seeking access to Starshield for operations inside Russia, but insisted that the reported disruption had nothing to do with the White House.
"Ukraine wants access to Starshield… in order to conduct deep strikes inside Russia. They do not have access to it at this moment. I don’t know what their theory is, but it has nothing to do with the White House. I saw a report the other day; it is categorically false. No one at the White House ordered the slowdown of the internet so certain drones couldn’t use it," he added.
Zelenskyy alleges disruption affected military operations
The controversy follows concerns over satellite connectivity disruptions that reportedly affected Ukrainian military operations as Russian attacks continued. According to Axios, Zelenskyy raised concerns about the impact of the disruptions on Ukraine's ability to defend itself.
In an interview with British broadcaster Piers Morgan on Piers Morgan Uncensored, Zelenskyy accused Musk of restricting Ukrainian access to Starlink and said the disruption had affected military operations.
"I am sure they knew what they did, absolutely," Zelenskyy said, referring to the reported disruption.
"Because it was 1 am at night, (when) Starlink was blocked by SpaceX and the United States," he added.
CNN reported that Ukrainian authorities were caught off guard by restrictions affecting Starshield. A Ukrainian military source with direct knowledge of the impact told the broadcaster, "The complications are substantial."
Ukrainian forces rely on Starlink connectivity to operate reconnaissance and interceptor drones, gather intelligence and carry out other battlefield activities. Any disruption to the service can therefore affect communications and the coordination of military operations.
Starlink connectivity reportedly being restored
Mykhailo Fedorov, former minister of defence of Ukraine, later said Starlink connectivity was being restored and called for the removal of restrictions affecting Starshield.
"Starlink connectivity at speeds of up to 160 km/h is being restored. Removing Starshield’s speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine’s defence. Thank you, Elon Musk. We hope for your continued support," Fedorov posted on X.
The dispute highlights Ukraine's reliance on satellite communications for its war effort and the influence that private technology providers can have on military operations. While US officials deny ordering a slowdown, questions remain over the reported disruption, the distinction between Starlink and Starshield, and the terms under which Ukraine can access these services.

stories.headline: Dussehra celebrated in Belagavi
stories.deck: Family members of the Patils of the old city performed the pooja. They received various palanquins carrying revered deities such as Venkatramna, Maruti, Jotiba, and the Aapti tree
stories.bodyText:
Dussehra festival was celebrated with joy and fervour in Belagavi on Tuesday (October 20, 2026). On Tuesday, the Simolanghana, a border-crossing ritual, was held at the Vidya Niketan grounds near St. Xavier’s School in Belagavi cantonment. It attracted people from all walks of life. The faithful exchanged leaves of the Shami tree (Prosopis cineraria) and Aapti tree (Bauhinia racemosa), in a symbolic gesture of exchanging gold as a mark of good will.
Family members of the Patils of the old city performed the pooja. They received various palanquins carrying revered deities such as Venkatramna, Maruti, Jotiba, and the Aapti tree.
This Utsav is believed to have been initiated by K.T. Pujari and Sons in 1901. It involves a procession featuring five magnificent Devi chariots, all culminating in the same grounds. They include those of Marriamma Devi, Muthu Mariamma, Kunti Devi, and Mariama from Telugu colony, who are believed to be sisters. Folk artists performed songs and dances.
The annual car festival or Rathotsava of Sri Venkat Ramana temple in Shahapur Vithaldev Galli was organised in the morning. This ritual is said to be 200 years old. Believers participated in Vaahanaotsav for eight days preceding Dussehra. The vaahans of the lord, in the forms of Tiger, Hanuman, Eagle, Peacock, Elephant, bull, crane and Horse were taken out. These were held near the Shahapur temple that has been managed by the Naik family for more than 200 years. “Before independence, the temple used to receive grants from the Nizam of Bijapur,” the organisers said.

stories.headline: Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper train likely to be launched on November 1
stories.deck: According to a Railway Board communication accessed by The Hindu, the service has been approved following the minutes of a meeting held on February 16, 2026
stories.bodyText:
The Bengaluru–Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper train is likely to be launched on November 1, coinciding with Karnataka Rajyotsava, with regular operations expected to begin the following day.
The service is proposed to run six days a week, although an official notification from the Railway Board is awaited. Sources in South Western Railway (SWR) said Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw is expected to flag off the service.
Once introduced, it will become the first Vande Bharat sleeper train to operate in southern India, providing an overnight rail connection between two major metropolitan cities.
According to a Railway Board communication accessed by The Hindu, the service was approved following the minutes of a meeting held on February 16, 2026. The Bengaluru–Mumbai service will operate as Train No. 27652, while the return journey from Mumbai will be numbered 27651.
As per the proposed timetable, Train No. 27652 will leave KSR Bengaluru at 10 p.m. and reach Dharmavaram at 12.50 a.m. and Wadi at 5.05 a.m. before arriving at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) in Mumbai at 1.50 p.m. the next day.
In the opposite direction, Train No. 27651 will depart CSMT at 10.30 p.m. and reach Wadi at 7.25 a.m. and Dharmavaram at 11.45 a.m. before terminating at KSR Bengaluru at 2.50 p.m.
The route will connect important railway stations in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Maharashtra.
The proposed operating pattern provides for the Bengaluru–Mumbai train to remain off service on Mondays and the Mumbai–Bengaluru train on Tuesdays. Two Vande Bharat sleeper trainsets will be deployed for the service, according to the Railway Board document.
Solapur and Pune have been designated for watering and other terminal-related requirements.
Focus on overnight travel
The new service is intended to provide a faster and more comfortable option for passengers travelling long distances overnight. Earlier, Mr. Vaishnaw had indicated that the Bengaluru–Mumbai sleeper service would be introduced soon and would mark the debut of the Vande Bharat sleeper variant in southern India.
India's first commercial Vande Bharat sleeper service commenced operations on January 22, 2026, between Kamakhya in Assam and Howrah in West Bengal. Operated by the Northeast Frontier Railway, the train covers approximately 972 km in around 14 hours.
Designed primarily for overnight journeys spanning 800 km to 1,200 km, Vande Bharat sleeper trains are intended to offer an alternative to conventional premium long-distance services, including Rajdhani Express trains, on selected routes.
A 16-coach Vande Bharat sleeper rake accommodates 823 passengers. It comprises 11 third AC coaches with 611 berths, four second AC coaches providing 188 berths, and one first AC coach with 24 berths.
The train features fully air-conditioned coaches, automatic sliding doors, CCTV surveillance, bio-vacuum toilets, sensor-operated water taps, individual reading lights, charging points, and digital passenger information display. Catering facilities will offer vegetarian and non-vegetarian meals.
Safety features include the indigenous Kavach automatic train protection system and emergency talk-back facilities. The driver cabins are air-conditioned and equipped with dedicated washrooms.
The final timetable and operational details are expected to be confirmed through the Railway Board's formal notification, according to officials.

stories.headline: Desk jobs, long commutes: Why women's pelvic health in trouble
stories.deck: Many young women in Bengaluru experience pelvic-floor issues related to long working hours and sedentary lifestyles. Medical professionals note that problems can stem from factors beyond pregnancy, such as obesity and chronic conditions. Women often normalize symptoms and avoid seeking timely medical help due to embarrassment and societal attitudes. Treatment options vary and may involve…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Holding your pee because you can't find a clean washroom or sitting at your desk for hours without a break could contribute to long-term pelvic-floor problems, warn doctors in the city, as more women, including those in their teens and twenties, are visiting OPDs with problems such as incontinence, pelvic pain, and painful intercourse.
Women who have never given birth can also develop dysfunction.
"We're seeing more young women with pelvic-floor symptoms, with greater awareness and willingness to seek medical help. Pregnancy and childbirth are important risk factors, as they can strain the pelvic-floor muscles, nerves and connective tissues. However, pelvic-floor dysfunction is not limited to women who have been pregnant or have given birth, nor is it synonymous with childbirth-related injury," said Dr Rubina Shanawaz, additional director of uro-gynaecology, gynec-oncology, laparoscopic & robotic surgery, Fortis Hospital, Cunningham Road.
She added, "Women who have never been pregnant can also develop problems such as an overactive or poorly coordinated pelvic floor, urinary urgency, pelvic pain, painful intercourse and difficulties with bowel movements."
What is causing these problems? Dr Prathima A, consultant-obstetrics, gynaecology and urogynaecology, Motherhood Hospitals, Banashankari, explained, "The corporate and tech-oriented nature of Bengaluru has contributed to pelvic-floor dysfunction among young women, with long hours at desks becoming an important factor. 
Sitting in offices for hours and commuting through city traffic for long periods can result in constant, passive strain on the pelvic region, with lifestyle factors playing as important a role as traditional causes."
Dr Varini N, senior consultant, obstetrics & gynaecology, Milann Fertility and Birthing Hospital, added, "Weight gain or obesity, chronic constipation and straining, reduced physical activity, high-impact exercise in some individuals, chronic coughing and certain musculoskeletal or neurological conditions can also contribute."
While awareness around these problems has increased, doctors said symptoms are still widely normalised and women often don't seek help early. "Many women normalise these symptoms because they associate them with ageing, menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth or simply being a woman. There can also be considerable embarrassment around discussing urine leakage, bowel symptoms or painful intercourse, so women may adapt their routines rather than seek help," Dr Varini said.
She added, "The problem with delaying assessment is that persistent symptoms can affect a lot more than physical health. Women may start avoiding exercise, long journeys, social activities or intimacy because they are worried about leakage, urgency or pain. In some cases, symptoms can also become more difficult to manage when the underlying problem is left unaddressed."
Although Kegel exercises, which target the pelvic floor, have become widely popular thanks to the internet, doctors warned that these exercises could do more harm than good if performed incorrectly. "Kegel exercises can help strengthen a weak pelvic floor, but they aren't right for everyone. In women with an overactive or tight pelvic floor, repeated contractions may worsen symptoms such as pelvic pain or pain during intercourse. Exercises should, therefore, be prescribed based on an assessment of symptoms and muscle function, rather than as a blanket approach," said Dr Rubina.
Dr Prathima added, "Pelvic-floor problems can have varied causes, including endometriosis, PID, STIs and declining estrogen. In younger women, urinary urgency and frequency may also stem from UTIs rather than muscle weakness. Treatment can involve pelvic-floor retraining, core exercises, biofeedback or medical intervention, making clinical assessment important before starting exercises such as Kegels."

stories.headline: How row over rent turned deadly for Bengaluru advocate: 'One gave cash, another pumped bullet into his head'
stories.deck: A 42-year-old advocate named B Manjunath was shot dead late on Sunday night in Whitefield. The incident occurred due to a dispute with his tenants, who had not paid rent for three months. Reports indicate that the confrontation escalated when one tenant shot Manjunath from behind while he was counting cash. Police have launched a manhunt for the suspects, who fled on separate motorcycles.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A 42-year-old advocate was shot dead at his residence in Pattandur Agrahara, Whitefield, late Sunday night, allegedly by two tenants working as delivery agents following a dispute over unpaid rent.
The suspects, identified as Pankaj Dube and Amit Kumar Dube, both from Bihar, had been living in a small room behind the house of B Manjunath for around one-and-a-half years. Police said the duo had not paid rent for three months.
Unpaid rent leads to confrontation
According to the police complaint lodged by Manjunath’s brother Muniraju, the advocate reprimanded the tenants over the pending rent on Sunday night. The confrontation is suspected to have led to the murder.
“First, they came near the house and spoke to Manjunath for some time. Saying they would return with the money, they went back. Around 11.45pm, one of them returned and called Manjunath out,” Muniraju said.
One tenant hands over cash, the other allegedly opens fire
A close relative, Akshay, said one of the suspects handed over the rent to Manjunath. As the advocate counted the cash, the other suspect allegedly approached him from behind and shot him in the head.
Manjunath was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared him dead despite attempts to revive him. 
He is survived by his wife and two minor children.
Deputy commissioner of police (Whitefield) Saiduly Adavat said police launched a manhunt for the suspects, who allegedly fled on separate motorcycles.
Another senior police officer said investigators had leads on the suspects’ whereabouts and were probing how they obtained the firearm.
Police probe source of illegal firearm
A senior officer expressed concern over the alleged use of an illegal pistol in the killing. Police will investigate where the weapon was purchased and whether the suspects’ associates or relatives possess other illegal firearms, the officer said.
Manjunath’s family has four siblings, and the family’s ancestral properties include extensive landholdings and buildings, police said.
 Advocates’ association seeks speedy investigation
Condemning the killing, Advocates’ Association Bengaluru president Subba Reddy said representatives of the organisation met police commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh and sought a speedy investigation.
The association also discussed the need for guidelines for private firms hiring workers from other states and for house owners renting accommodation to them, he said.
Manjunath’s neighbour Siddegowda expressed shock over the incident and called for measures to prevent similar attacks.
 Killing follows shooting over business dispute
The murder comes a week after a realtor allegedly shot and injured his former car driver near Konanakunte over a business dispute. The realtor allegedly fired a round into the driver’s leg using his licensed revolver. Police arrested him and seized the weapon. The driver is recovering in hospital.

briefs.headline: Karnataka HC refuses to drop charge of culpable homicide not amounting murder against father in fatal accident caused by minor son
briefs.deck: Justice M. Nagaprasanna made these observations while dismissing a criminal petition filed by Nadeem of Mysuru, who sought to quash the charge sheet against him
briefs.bodyText:
Expressing concern over accidents caused by minor-driven vehicles and emphasising parental accountability in use of vehicles by minors, the High Court of Karnataka has refused to discharge a father from the charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder after his 14-year-old son drove a car and caused a fatal accident that claimed three lives of a family.
“The message of the law must equally be unambiguous. A parent who knowingly places the steering wheel in the hands of a child cannot always retreat behind the minority of that child, when the adventure ends in catastrophe. Parenthood carries not merely affection and authority, but responsibility. Roads are shared public spaces, not training grounds for unlawful indulgence,” the Court said.
Further, the Court said that “when parental indulgence knowingly permits a child incapable in law of driving to command a machine capable of causing death, and precious lives are consequently lost, the law is entitled to inquire, upon evidence, whether the conduct was merely negligent or had crossed the frontier into culpable knowledge. That enquiry, in the case at hand, deserves a trial and not a premature burial at the stage of discharge.”
Justice M. Nagaprasanna made these observations while dismissing a criminal petition filed by Nadeem of Mysuru, who sought to quash the charge sheet against him under Section 304 Part-II (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The petition was restricted solely against the charge of culpable homicide, which attracts imprisonment up to 10 years, as the petitioner did not challenge the other connected offences, attracting lesser punishments.
The incident occurred on December 10, 2020, when the petitioner’s minor son allegedly took a car for a drive. The vehicle, driven at high speed and with negligence, lost control, hit a road divider, and collided with a motorcycle. The crash resulted in the deaths of a couple, including their five-year-old child, while another child sustained injuries.
Initially, a case was registered for rash and negligent driving but after investigation the police invoked the charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder against for the petitioner.
The petitioner had contended that his son took the car without his knowledge or consent and that, at best, the material could only support a charge of negligence, not culpable homicide, which requires knowledge that the act was likely to cause death.
However, the Court noted that the charge sheet materials indicate that the petitioner was in the habit of permitting his minor son to drive the car repeatedly, himself had handed over the keys to his 14-year-old son on that day of the incident.
The Court noted that the petitioner was not behind the wheel, but the alleged act of ‘consciously entrusting’ a vehicle to a legally incompetent child is a positive act that could attract the requisite knowledge.
“If a parent consciously places a motor vehicle in the hands of a 14-year-old child, knowing fully well that the child is legally incompetent and manifestly unequipped to drive it upon a public road, the question whether such conduct carries with it the requisite knowledge of likely fatal consequences cannot be foreclosed at the threshold stage of trial,” the Court observed while pointing out that a trial essential in this case to establish, or otherwise, the charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
Noticing that Karnataka recorded 751 such accidents involving minors during 2025-26, Justice Nagaprasanna said, “the rising incidence of such accidents, therefore, reinforces the need for courts to exercise circumspection before interdicting a prosecution at its threshold where the charge sheet itself contains material, prima facie, indicating conscious entrustment of the vehicle to a minor.”

briefs.headline: Greater Bengaluru Authority receives over 1,500 objections to tree felling for Hebbal Short Tunnel
briefs.deck: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) restrained the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) from felling any trees till the hearing in the case challenging tree felling for the project is completed
briefs.bodyText:
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has received more than 1,500 objections against the felling of 1,128 trees for the Hebbal Short Tunnel Project, even as the National Green Tribunal (NGT) restrained the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) from felling any trees till the hearing in the case challenging tree felling for the project is completed.
The GBA had invited objections to the proposed tree felling on September 20, giving a 10-day deadline. However, the authority did not upload the list of tree species, prompting activists to demand an extension.
According to GBA sources, they got over 700 objections during the first window, with the remaining objections coming in before the final deadline.
The officer told The Hindu that the major objections concerned species diversity and the sheer number of trees proposed to be felled. “Many objections are very detailed and include a list of species to highlight biodiversity. Many have also pointed out one aspect, like microclimate, and elaborated on the impact of cutting trees for that aspect,” the officer said.
Biodiversity loss and more
According to the officer, several objections also concern the size of certain trees, based on independent assessments by those who submitted them. Other objections highlight the potential impact on other species, hydrological concerns owing to the alignment’s proximity to Hebbal Lake, and the risk of the area turning into a heat island, as it serves as a key lung space.
The officer said the objections were being filtered and grouped under different themes. “We will send all the objections and concerns raised by citizens to the tree expert committee and the implementing agency, the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA).
“The BDA will also review the objections and explain why the trees need to be felled. A joint inspection of the site will also be conducted by the tree expert committee members and the BDA to review the proposal,” he said.
Meanwhile, due to an NGT stay order the BDA cannot fell any trees until December 15, the next date of hearing. Further action can be taken only after the hearing and in accordance with its outcome.
Tree committee to decide
Recently, during an interaction with The Hindu, BDA Chairperson N.A. Haris had said that only 56 trees would be felled and the remaining trees would be translocated. However, the GBA officer clarified that any decision regarding the trees would have to be taken by the tree expert committee.
“Irrespective of whether the trees are translocated or felled, the BDA will have to plant 10 trees for every tree cleared,” the GBA official said.

briefs.headline: Sugarcane farmers crisis: Karnataka CM Shivakumar seeks Centre’s intervention
briefs.deck: State will fulfil some of their demands, says Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
briefs.bodyText:
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has sought the urgent intervention of the Union government in resolving the crisis faced by sugarcane farmers.
In a letter to the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Chief Minister presented a list of demands that include policy changes and focussed action. He also assured that the State government would fulfil some of their demands including monitoring of sugar factories.
On the day the Centre announced excluding sugarcane based ethanol from the tenders by oil companies, the CM asked the government to reconsider its decision.
The CM asked PM Modi to revise Minimum Selling Price (MSP) for sugar that has remained unchanged since 2019, restore the base recovery rate for Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) at 9.5% and to reconsider the exclusion of sugarcane-based ethanol from procurement tenders. He also sought an increase in the price of sugarcane-based ethanol.
“The Minimum Selling Price (MSP) of sugar has remained at ₹31 per kg since February 14, 2019, whereas the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane has increased from ₹2,750 to ₹3,650 per tonne. Given the sugar price levels of 2019, sugar mills are unable to pay the fair price for sugarcane. Therefore, the Minimum Selling Price (MSP) of sugar should be revised,” he said.
Forwarding a request from farmers associations, the CM requested a policy change to fix separate MSPs for domestic and commercial sugar. "This would protect domestic consumers while ensuring that bulk commercial buyers pay a fair price and ensure higher profits for sugar mills, so that they could pay higher prices to farmers.”
“In the tender issued by Oil Marketing Companies on October 16, 2026, for the 2026-27 period (November 2026 to October 2027), ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup, and B-heavy molasses has been excluded, whereas ethanol produced from C-heavy molasses remains eligible. Karnataka possesses an annual production capacity of 225 crore liters of sugarcane-based ethanol.”
“The exclusion of these raw materials is likely to adversely affect the revenue of sugar mills and diminish their ability to make timely payments to sugarcane farmers. Therefore, this decision should be reconsidered, and a fair allocation should be provided for the production of ethanol from sugarcane-based raw materials, in line with the established capacities of the mills,” he said.
“Although there is an annual increase in the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) payable for sugarcane, the prices for ethanol produced from sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses have remained unchanged since 2022-23. In contrast, the prices for grain-based ethanol have increased over the last few years. Therefore, the price of sugarcane-based ethanol should be appropriately revised to offset the rising costs of sugarcane,” the letter said.
“Earlier, the base recovery rate to calculate the FRP was 9.50%. But it was increased in stages to 10.25%. When the recovery rate falls below this base level, the FRP is reduced. But then, sugar recovery depends on factors such as soil, climate, and the timing of sugarcane crushing, factors that are beyond the control of farmers. Consequently, farmers in regions with lower recovery rates do not receive the base FRP. Therefore, the base recovery rate should be reset to 9.50%,’’ CM Shivakumar said.
The CM welcomed the panel headers by farm scientist Ramesh Chand to look into the issues of farmers. “The State will participate fully in the committee’s activities and share data. However, as the sugarcane crushing season in Karnataka is already delayed, farmers are awaiting an urgent assurance from the Union government. Certain decisions can be taken immediately, even as the committee continues its work,’’ he said.
“The State government, on its part, will take all necessary measures to protect the interests of sugarcane growers. These include the installation of digital load cells to prevent irregularities in weighing at sugar factories, monthly inspections by district-level teams, and directives for laboratories to obtain National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL). However, the farmers’ primary demands can only be met by the Government of India, and therefore, we seek your intervention,” the CM said.
CM Shivakumar said he had tried to persuade farmers to withdraw their agitation in Belagavi by visiting them in Kittur and by holding meetings with Pralhad Joshi, Union Food Minister. The farmers have said that their primary demands are before the Union government and that they will not call off their agitation unless they receive an assurance from the Centre. Due to these protests, the sugarcane crushing season has not yet commenced in North Karnataka. Sugarcane that is ready for harvest remains standing in the fields; with every passing day of delay, there is a loss in both the weight of the cane and its sugar content. “Protests and road blocks by sugarcane farmers are disrupting public order and causing severe inconvenience to the general public,” he said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru hospital urges women to make breast awareness a monthly habit
briefs.deck: Launches ‘Left Right Kiya Kya?’ campaign to promote three-minute monthly check and timely medical advice
briefs.bodyText:
A Bengaluru-based private hospital has launched a campaign encouraging women to make breast awareness part of their monthly routine, with a simple reminder to look for changes, become familiar with how their breasts normally feel, and seek medical advice if anything unusual is noticed.
The nationwide campaign, ‘Left Right Kiya Kya?’, was launched by HCG Cancer Hospitals with the aim of extending breast cancer awareness beyond October, when campaigns typically focus on the disease. It encourages women to spend three minutes every month paying attention to both breasts.
According to the International Agency for Research on Cancer’s GLOBOCAN 2024 estimates cited by the hospital, India recorded about 2.37 lakh new breast cancer cases and 96,100 deaths in 2024. Breast cancer accounts for about 30% of new cancer diagnoses among women in the country.
The campaign uses the familiar words ‘left’ and ‘right’ as a reminder to check both breasts and recognise unusual changes. It includes music and an AI-generated film featuring women in everyday situations. An on-ground activation at Nexus Seawoods in Navi Mumbai featured a live musical performance by women dressed in pink, followed by a doctor’s demonstration on recognising breast changes.
Recognising changes
The campaign encourages women to look for changes in breast size, shape or skin, check for unusual changes around the breasts or nipples, and become familiar with how their breasts and underarm areas normally feel.
Jayanti Thumsi, Group Lead, Robotic Breast Surgery, at the hospitals, said some women sought medical help only when their cancer was advanced, while others noticed changes but did not act on them.
“Most breast changes are not cancer, but they should never be ignored. If you notice a lump, unusual nipple discharge, or any other change, consult a doctor without delay, rather than waiting for your next monthly reminder,” she said.
She added that breast awareness did not replace screening, and mammograms should be planned according to age and individual risk.
Manu Sankar Das, Chief Marketing Officer, HCG Cancer Hospitals, said the campaign was designed to make breast awareness a recurring habit rather than an annual reminder.
“Awareness that lasts only through October isn’t enough. It needs to become a reminder that comes back every month. Left breast. Right breast. Three minutes, once a month,” he said.

briefs.headline: How this Bengaluru bookstore is reviving the practice of writing letters
briefs.deck: The Sunday Letter Project, which began in 2025, is a global initiative with ‘letter keepers’ across the world with Beku Books in JP Nagar Bengaluru as the only participating letter keeper from India. We find out what it is all about
briefs.bodyText:
The Sunday Letter Project aims to revive the art of handwritten letters in the digital age. Every week participants from across the world write one letter . Founded in 2025 by Rebecca and Karl of Wildflower Illustration Co in England, the project is a community writing initiative.
In the Sunday Letter Project’s database, the only listed Letter-Keeper from India is Bengaluru’s Beku Books located in JP Nagar.
Letter-Keeper shops act as the regional address for the participants. They ship letters abroad to the other letter-keepers, and receive letters from across the world. They also hold them until the intended recipients collect their letters. This method helps people find pen-pals from across the world without sharing their home addresses.
This initiative is completely free and acts as a shop-to-shop letter writing movement, replicating the Poste Restante system (where a post office holds letters and packages until the recipient collects them in person). Each participant can write an introductory letter with basic information about themselves attaching their letter-keeper’s address. This letter will join a pool of letters across the listed shops for other participants to choose and reply.
One can also choose to respond to introductory letters by others in the pool.
“It started off as a pledge to write a letter every Sunday,” says Premsakhi Mokkapati, head curator at Beku Books. “A customer can walk in and read a letter; they can photograph the letter and return address and choose to write back to them. Introductory letters are kept at the bookstores so a person can have more than one pen pal.”
After starting their project in Bengaluru through Beku Books, Sunday Letter Project has received a good response from the frequent customers at the store. “Our customers are also sending letters to people across the world, and picking up responses. We hold on to their letters until they are able to come and pick them up.”
Beku Books came across this initiative on social media; they submitted the required form and paid a small yearly fee to cover the administrative charges. Upon approval from the Sunday Letter Project founders, their bookstore is listed among the participating shops from across the globe.
“We have received messages from people around India asking if they could send us letters as well. It feels nice to be doing something that no one else is , but we are also planning to conduct a few events to encourage more people to write letters.”
The central intent behind this initiative is to bring back the practice of physical writing.
Having said this, she mentions the few rules of the Sunday Letter Project — one should not include personal details including phone numbers, addresses or social media handles. Self-promotion or advertising is not allowed and letters should always be kind and respectful.
For more information visit thesundayletterproject.com or @beku.blr on Instagram

briefs.headline: Meet Goofy, the winner of the Fat Dogs of Bengaluru contest
briefs.deck: Held through an online poll, the Fat Dogs of Bengaluru competition is donating proceeds to animal rights groups like CARE. Among 64 contenders and two lakh votes, Goofy emerged the winner
briefs.bodyText:
It was a fierce fight for the top spot of Fat Dogs of Bengaluru this weekend. Bachonker McChonketh from Neon Market in Indiranagar was going up against Goofy who hails from Nagarbhavi. Ultimately Goofy took the crown of the fattest dog in Bengaluru after six knockout rounds and an online poll that received more than two lakh votes.
The Fat Dogs of Bengaluru initiative is styled after the Fat Dogs of Delhi contest that was held a few weeks ago online. It garnered a lot of attention, and Gola from Hauz Khas, who unfortunately passed away, won the title posthumously.
Mazin Mohamed Iqbal is the product marketing manager at Fave, a UPI app aimed at gen-z, which was the driving force behind the initiative here in the city. “We saw the Delhi contest became a viral phenomenon and we thought let us replicate it in Bengaluru. It is something fun that we can involve the community in.” Mazin also runs an Instagram page called Fave Finds Bengaluru. “We go around the city, and we make videos about the most interesting things in Bengaluru.” They started the page @fatdogsofblr and invited entries at the end of September.
People were asked to send in a picture of their street dog, a name and the area where the dog lives in. “A lot of people responded. Within five days we received hundreds of entries. 64 dogs were chosen for the contest.” The website fatdogsofblr was created in association with Emergent, an AI software creation platform. The tournament unfolded online and this past weekend was the final face off between Bachonker McChonketh and Goofy. Their page is not monetised and they do not do any paid promotions, Mazin clarifies.
Heated rivalry
Canines from all across the city were up for contention. Mr Gundumani from SP Road went head-to-head with Vasu from RR Nagar. Jonathan Joestar from Sahakarnagar emerged a fan favourite, with critical comments accusing vote rigging (how topical) when he lost out in the semi finals. LPG, Old Monk, Fattet Bhature, Overlord of Gluttony and Chonky Shastry were some of the other entrants. The website has a dog map where you can zoom into different areas and see the dogs who live on those streets.
For a cause
The Fat Dogs of Bengaluru initiative is not only for fun. Emergent has pledged a donation to Charlie’s Animal Rescue Centre (C.A.R.E.). Fave is also donating ₹1000 for every 100 downloads of their app. Some users have raised concerns that contests like this promote unhealthiness or obesity in dogs. To this Mazin says, “I think we can appreciate all dogs. Recording and taking pictures of these dogs does not mean we are condoning it. We also hope that through this, these dogs gain more attention, and get medical help, if they need it.”
