briefs.headline: Car not a toy, says HC; dad to face trial for crash by minor that killed 3
briefs.deck: Following a devastating incident, a father contested the Karnataka high court's ruling regarding culpable homicide charges linked to his 14-year-old son's reckless driving. The accident claimed three lives, leading the court to stress the perils of allowing minors to operate vehicles and affirm the importance of parents being accountable. The father's attempt to cancel the charges was ultimately…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A car cannot become a toy in the hands of underage children, Karnataka high court observed, refusing to quash culpable homicide proceedings against a Mysuru resident whose 14-year-old son caused an accident that left three members of a family dead in Dec 2020.
"The steering wheel of a motor vehicle cannot become a plaything in the hands of a child, nor can a public road become the playground for such indulgence," Justice M Nagaprasanna observed in his order dated Oct 16, stressing that parental responsibility cannot be evaded when a minor is willingly allowed to drive.
The petitioner's son was driving a Volkswagen Vento, entrusted to his father by his employer, when the accident took place on old Bengaluru-Mysuru road, killing a couple and their five-year-old son.
The petitioner, Nadeem-Ur-Rehman, had challenged the rejection of his discharge plea by a trial court and had sought the quashing of proceedings against him under IPC section 304 Part-II, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder. He was also facing allegations of other traffic violations.
Karnataka recorded 751 accidents involving minors in 2025-26
The petitioner contended that his son took the vehicle out without his knowledge. 
The case could, at best, be an offence based on rashness or negligence, but could not be elevated to culpable homicide, he further argued.
Opposing the plea, the public prosecutor submitted that the material on record indicated the petitioner had handed the car keys to his son and permitted him to drive. He said this had allegedly happened on earlier occasions as well.
A parent who knowingly hands car keys to a child cannot “retreat behind the minority of that child when the adventure ends in catastrophe”, HC observed. The question of whether a parent’s conduct was negligence or culpable knowledge could be decided at the trial, it said. Quoting statistics, Justice Nagaprasanna noted that Karnataka recorded 751 accidents involving minors in 2025-26, standing at sixth place among all states.

stories.headline: Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger a 'good idea', special committees formed for talks
stories.deck: SpaceX shares rose 4.9% in extended trading following the remarks. Speculation about a potential deal has grown in recent weeks, with Barclays suggesting last week that an announcement could come before Tesla's annual meeting in December. Musk has previously floated the idea, pointing to increasing overlap between the businesses. The merger discussions came as SpaceX reported its first profit as…
stories.bodyText:
Elon Musk
’s business empire could be heading towards a major consolidation, with 
SpaceX
 and Tesla setting up special committees to discuss a possible merger. Musk confirmed the talks on Tuesday, saying he viewed combining the two companies favourably, although any deal would depend on the committees’ deliberations and approval from shareholders.
"I think it would be a good idea, but it's really up to the special committees of both companies," Musk said, in the first official confirmation that the companies were formally talking. "Because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussion of the special committees," he told investors on a conference call as per news agency Reuters. Shareholders ultimately would need to approve a deal, he added.
SpaceX shares rose 4.9% in extended trading following the remarks. Speculation about a potential deal has grown in recent weeks, with Barclays suggesting last week that an announcement could come before Tesla's annual meeting in December. Musk has previously floated the idea, pointing to increasing overlap between the businesses.
SpaceX posts first public-company profit as AI revenue surges
The merger discussions came as SpaceX reported its first profit as a public company, alongside a sharp rise in revenue from artificial intelligence (AI). 
Revenue increased 161% year-on-year to $14.58 billion in the three months ended September 30.
AI revenue surged almost tenfold to $7.56 billion, largely driven by renting data-centre computing capacity to developers such as Anthropic, Google's parent Alphabet and Reflection AI, rather than by sales from its own AI models.
"We are in an inflection moment for SpaceX across launch, connectivity and superintelligence," Musk said on the call. He ended his portion of prepared remarks with a seemingly off-script remark. "In a nutshell, what this implies for SpaceX annual recurring revenue by the end of '27 is somewhere between $500 billion and a trillion."
SpaceX chief financial officer Bret Johnsen reiterated that the company expected annual recurring revenue of about $100 billion by the end of 2026. The company plans to spend $35 billion to $40 billion on capital expenditure in the fourth quarter. AI accounted for $16.4 billion of its $19.6 billion in capital spending in the third quarter, with investment in computing infrastructure nearly tripling.
SpaceX reported net income of $4.4 billion, compared with a loss of $1.1 billion a year earlier. The result also beat analysts' average expectation of a $1.57 billion profit. On an adjusted per-share basis, the company earned 45 cents, above the average estimate of 13 cents, according to IBES calculations.
"SpaceX delivered the quarter the bulls wanted, at least on the top line," said Will Rhind, CEO of asset manager GraniteShares. "The story now is all about AI. The compute contracts signed earlier this year are turning into revenue faster than a lot of people thought."
Starlink growth and Starship remain key to long-term plans
SpaceX's expanding AI business includes Grok, social media platform X and its growing data-centre operations. However, the AI unit has incurred large operating losses, and the company has warned that sustained investment will be needed before it can generate consistent profits.
"With AI revenue now the company's biggest business line, the company's hyperscale business is quickly providing operating strength and leverage which will carry into the advancements of its satellite and launch business," said Daniel Newman, CEO of tech research group the Futurum Group. "Increasingly, the strength and diversification of SpaceX makes a merger with Tesla feel imminent."
Starlink, SpaceX's satellite internet business, also continued to expand. It had 13.6 million subscribers in the third quarter, exceeding analysts' expectation of 12.19 million. However, average monthly revenue per subscriber fell from $99 in 2023 to $69 in the latest quarter as the company expanded into more markets with cheaper plans. SpaceX has warned that entering countries with lower purchasing power could push average revenue per user down further.
The company's longer-term plans also depend on Starship, its next-generation reusable rocket system, which has yet to enter commercial service. The rocket is expected to help deploy more advanced Starlink satellites and support plans for AI computing infrastructure in orbit.
SpaceX successfully deployed several Starlink satellites last month during Starship's first orbital test flight, although the flight ended hours earlier than expected following an engine issue. While Falcon rocket launches remain active across commercial and government missions, Starship development continues to involve significant costs and uncertainty.
SpaceX has also increasingly prioritised launching satellites for its own network over carrying third-party payloads. The combination of a growing AI business, expanding satellite connectivity and ambitious rocket development has changed the company's financial profile, making the potential merger with Tesla a significant development for both businesses.
(With inputs from Reuters)

BENGALURU: Indian technology professionals are increasingly looking for employers that offer hands-on artificial intelligence (AI) experience and clearly defined career paths, while multinational global capability centres (GCCs) are emerging as the preferred next career move for many, according to a Talent500 survey. Talent500 is part of ANSR, which has set up more than 200 GCCs in India.
Thesurvey of 2,000 technology, product and data professionals found that 71% wanted hands-on AI upskilling, but only 29% said their employers provided it. Career growth was another major concern: 87% said clearly defined career paths were very important when evaluating an employer, while 79% said they would abandon an application or decline an offer if growth opportunities were unclear.
The gap is also visible in employees’ current workplaces. Only 46% of respondents described their career paths as very clear. GCCs were the first choice for the next career move for 69% of respondents, ahead of Indian product companies at 37% and IT services and outsourcing firms at 28%. Career growth was the leading factor in evaluating a GCC, cited by 48%, followed by the global parent brand at 41%, India-centre leadership and culture at 36%, and exposure to AI and technology at 33%. stories.headline: Moves by the North of England to unlock India trade
stories.deck: Regional partnerships can help businesses unlock the potential of the India-U.K. trade pact
stories.bodyText:
The India-United Kingdom Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) has opened the door to a new phase in the relationship between the two countries, with the focus now shifting from agreement to action. The momentum is already being seen, as the leaders from across the North of England have been travelling together to India, for the first time under The Great North banner to strengthen ties on trade, investment, innovation, culture and the visitor economy.
Editorial | Maturing approach: On the India-U.K. Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
Beyond headlines
Agreements are only as powerful as the opportunities they unlock. Tariff reductions, regulatory alignment, and mobility provisions matter enormously; yet, their true value is realised only when businesses on the ground understand precisely where and how they apply. Keeping this in mind, the Northern Mayors were joined by businesses, small and medium enterprises and universities from across the region to help bolster links, showcase the North’s economic assets and create new opportunities for trade, investment and academic collaboration. The North of England and India already have deep and growing ties, with nearly 5,40,000 people of Indian origin living across the region. Indian companies have invested over £1bn in the Northwest alone, supporting more than 6,700 jobs, according to the Confederation of Indian Industry report. Nearly 200 delegates from across the North were part of the visit, bringing together mayors, businesses, universities and leaders from tourism, culture and sport to make the case for the North as a destination for investment, partnerships and growth.
U.K. Foreign Secretary David Lammy’s statement (made in 2024) describing the trade pact as “the floor, not the ceiling” of the bilateral relationship is the true essence of the current ties between New Delhi and London. The agreement is the result of several rounds of negotiations, over the years — 14 rounds of discussions, with each point deliberated to deliver and cash-in on strengths and individual goals of the two nations.
The U.K. India Business Council, a mission partner for the Great North delegation, is working to help U.K. businesses better understand the opportunity and reframe how they see India. India is no longer simply a market to sell into. It is a strategic partner with the potential to become an integral part of the U.K.’s research and development (R and D), technology, talent and supply chains.
Visits to action
In the last few years, the ministerial and government visits have been largely with a broader vision to keep the ball rolling. This was seen with former U.K. Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer’s delegation coming to India in 2025 and vice-versa. But this time we see policymakers coming in to discuss the next steps. Government meetings, business delegations, university partnerships, R and D collaborations, sports and cultural ties and targeted regional engagements in business hubs of India. The itinerary was designed to build a long-term relationship.
There is already some impact, with the footprint of Indian businesses in the U.K. having expanded sharply this year, the number of Indian-owned companies rising nearly 60% from the previous year and combined revenues surpassing £105 billion, according to the latest India Meets Britain Tracker published by Grant Thornton UK.
Bilateral trade between India and the U.K. rose to £47.4 billion in 2025, marking an 11.7% increase from the previous year. Growth was concentrated on advanced manufacturing, clean energy and technology. With the CETA now in place, the India-U.K. corridor is poised for unprecedented growth, creating value for both economies.
In one of the U.K. India Business Council (UKIBC)’s reports on the CETA, it has focused on regional collaboration, mapping them against the sector-specific pathways for growth. A regional approach to trade engagement offers India a nuanced and targeted pathway into the U.K. economy; one that goes beyond London and into the innovation-rich heartlands of Britain. The report takes one step ahead from the macro view and delves into specifics. Examine Maharashtra’s aerospace ambitions, Gujarat’s chemical exports, Karnataka’s world-class IT ecosystem and Tamil Nadu’s pharmaceutical prowess. It asks not just what this deal means for India or the U.K. in aggregate, but also what it means for the industries and communities that will live with its consequences day to day.
Conversations need to translate into business. For a micro, small and medium enterprise, the challenge is often not whether the benefits of a trade agreement exist, but how one can access them. That means understanding and navigating the finer details, such as knowing that a tariff preference exists, establishing whether a product qualifies, meeting rules of origin, securing the right documentation, and managing the administrative costs of claiming the benefit. It can be seen as an empowering process.
Business guide
As India signs more trade agreements, the task is about ensuring businesses can take full advantage of what has been negotiated on their behalf. To simplify this, the UKIBC has developed a U.K.-India CETA Business Utilisation Manual — A Practical Activation Guide for Indian and UK Businesses, which was launched recently by Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal in London. The guide is designed to simplify the agreement and help businesses understand where the opportunities lie, whether they qualify, and how to act on them.
Kishore Jayaraman is the Group CEO of the UK India Business Council (UKIBC). He has been the India Chair of UKIBC and a Member of the UKIBC Group Board since 2016, and is also the former President of Rolls-Royce, India and South Asia

stories.headline: Amazon targets Nvidia’s software edge with new AI tool
stories.deck: Open-source TorchNeuron aims to make it easier for developers to shift AI workloads to Amazon’s Trainium chips without rewriting code
stories.bodyText:
U.S.-based technology company Amazon has launched an open-source software tool that allows developers to run existing AI code on its own AI chips with minimal changes, making it easier to switch hardware.
The initiative targets a software advantage that has helped Nvidia maintain its position in AI computing.
In an announcement published on its official news website on October 20, Amazon said its cloud-computing arm, Amazon Web Services (AWS), had developed TorchNeuron, a tool that allows developers to run AI workloads built using PyTorch on its Trainium2 and Trainium3 chips with minimal code changes.
PyTorch is an open-source machine-learning framework widely used to develop and train AI models. Amazon estimates that 85% of AI researchers and developers use it. TorchNeuron is designed to let developers use familiar PyTorch code and tools on Trainium, potentially reducing the engineering work involved in moving workloads to alternative hardware.
“85% of AI developers write their code in PyTorch. But until now, trying a new chip meant rewriting and revalidating work that took months to perfect. That’s an enormous tax on teams who should be building products, not porting code,” AWS chief executive Matt Garman said.
“Today we’re changing that. TorchNeuron runs your existing PyTorch code natively on Trainium with a single config change. No rewrite. No revalidation. We’re open sourcing it under Apache 2.0, and we’re contributing the changes upstream to PyTorch itself, so the whole framework gets more hardware-agnostic for everyone.
“Developers should pick hardware on price, performance, and availability. Not because they’re locked in by code they already wrote,” he said.
The move addresses a key challenge for companies developing alternatives to Nvidia’s graphics processing units (GPUs).
NVIDIA’s CUDA platform provides the software tools and libraries that allow developers to run AI workloads on its GPUs. Its integration with frameworks such as PyTorch has helped build a broad developer ecosystem. Amazon says moving workloads to alternative chips can require substantial rewriting and revalidation, a barrier TorchNeuron is designed to reduce.
TorchNeuron is being released under the Apache 2.0 open-source licence as a public beta. Amazon is also contributing changes to PyTorch to reduce hardware-specific code in the framework, with the aim of making it easier to run AI workloads across different chips.
The unveiling has drawn support from Meta’s PyTorch engineering team. Jana Van Greunen, director of PyTorch engineering at Meta, said native support for Trainium would give researchers and engineers greater choice while allowing them to continue using familiar execution and distributed-computing tools.
Hugging Face, whose libraries are widely used to access and run AI models, has integrated support for Amazon’s Trainium chips into its Transformers and Diffusers libraries. The company said the new backend would let developers use familiar model definitions on Trainium, reducing the need to maintain separate, hardware-specific implementations.
Amazon said more than 30 early customers across areas including robotics, voice AI and world models were using the software.

BENGALURU: Classrooms have been carved out of office space inside a WeWork building on Bannerghatta Road in Bengaluru. A postgraduate timetable runs from noon to 8 pm, fitting study blocks around time for building businesses. Shrey Doshi (25), a postgraduate alumnus, walks in with a blue drink. “That’s my product. Try it,” he says, before explaining the blue spirulina and tender coconut.
This is Mesa School of Business, where students must build businesses and find paying customers. Elsewhere, engineering clubs and laboratories offer another route into entrepreneurship. Across campuses, the support founders need ranges from time away from classes to equipment, early funding and introductions to buyers.
“The clearest difference comes from two things: time to build and access to infrastructure,” said Richa Bajpai of Campus Fund, which invests in student-led businesses. She cited BITS Pilani’s attendance flexibility and option to take time off to build as reasons it remained among the leading institutions supplying pitches to her fund. “Students who start companies still face rigid exam schedules and attendance rules that force a choice between their degree and their company,” she said.
Incubators also give young companies access to equipment they could not afford themselves,
Colleges also need to let students learn across disciplines, she added. For technical businesses, support can be tangible. IIT Jammu gave MachFly Aerospace labs, resources and early financial support to build its first prototype, Bajpai said. Incubators also give young companies access to equipment they could not afford themselves, professors with domain expertise and alumni with industry experience, she said.
Bajpai points to govt grants, competitions and cloud credits as starting points for founders without family money or business connections. She also cited Human Biogenesis, whose founders came from humble backgrounds and started at BioNEST, IIT Guwahati’s incubator.
The company has since completed clinical trials, raised aseed round and is moving into production, she said. At IIT Madras, director V Kamakoti described Centre for Innovation as “run by the student for the student”. Design clubs can feed into prototype development, with incubators, faculty and alumni supporting student teams. Citing Ather Energy’s journey, he spoke of “12 to 13 years of gestation” and the need for patient capital.
Other businesses can test demand sooner. Campus Fundbacked Mumbai Pav Co began with Mesa classmates Tanay Agarwal and Jash Arora making food in another operator’s kitchen and selling to business customers before opening a store, Agarwal said. He already knew his family’s restaurant businesses; Arora brought culinary training. Access is uneven. Mesa’s advertised four-year undergraduate programme costs Rs 48 lakh, excluding accommodation and overseas immersions. It does not award a university degree.

briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The Centre is set to review the National Mineral Policy, 2019, to align it with evolving sector demands, focusing on key priorities such as critical minerals, recycling, and deep-sea resources, according to people in the know.
The mines ministry has decided to constitute a panel to undertake a comprehensive review of the policy in the light of recent developments and emerging requirements. The nine-member committee will be chaired by the additional secretary in the mines ministry, they said. The panel has been asked to submit its recommendations within two months of its constitution.
The National Mineral Policy, 2019, was approved by the Union cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It was aimed at ensuring more effective regulation and sustainable development of the mining sector, and addressing the concerns of project-affected persons, particularly those living in tribal areas.
The policy sought to create a more effective, meaningful and implementable framework by bringing in greater transparency, better regulation and enforcement, balanced social and economic growth, and sustainable mining practices. It also included provisions to boost the mining sector, such as measures to encourage exploration, attract private investment, promote ease of doing business and ensure sustainable mining.

briefs.headline: Hotel tariffs in Delhi, Mumbai top Rishikesh, Ranthambore
briefs.deck: Leading hospitality consulting firm Hotelivate’s recently released trends & opportunities report for 2026 shows average revenue per available room (RevPAR) for Delhi at Rs 9,811; Mumbai Rs 9,761; Ranthambore Rs 9,649 and Rishikesh Rs 9,583 in FY 2025-26. In the previous fiscal, the top four positions were Ranthambore (Rs 0,059), Rishikesh (Rs 9,493), Mumbai (Rs 9,458) and Delhi (Rs 8,846).
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: For the first time since Covid, the leisure and spiritual destinations — Ranthambore and Rishikesh — have been overtaken by Mumbai and Delhi as the Indian cities with highest average hotel tariffs. Leading hospitality consulting firm Hotelivate’s recently released trends & opportunities report for 2026 shows average revenue per available room (RevPAR) for Delhi at Rs 9,811; Mumbai Rs 9,761; Ranthambore Rs 9,649 and Rishikesh Rs 9,583 in FY 2025-26.
In the previous fiscal, the top four positions were Ranthambore (Rs 0,059), Rishikesh (Rs 9,493), Mumbai (Rs 9,458) and Delhi (Rs 8,846).
This shows a revival in corporate travel, international visitation and the group-oriented Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions (MICE) activity. Varanasi has shown a big jump in average tariffs with the holy city boasting of the fifth highest rates at Rs 8,857 — ahead of Udaipur (Rs 8,414) and Goa (Rs 7,614) — in FY26, up from the ninth spot in previous fiscal when its RevPAR was Rs 6,769.
The deadly Pahalgam terror attack last April saw Srinagar register its biggest fall in visitors. “Srinagar recorded the sharpest decline across the dataset, with RevPAR falling 51.9% year-on-year (to Rs 3,323 in FY 26) and the market moving from among the country’s leading performers to the bottom 15. 
Jalandhar, Jammu and Amritsar faced similar pressures, as cancellations associated with Operation Sindoor weakened demand across markets closer to the border,” says the report.
At the end of March 2026, India had a pipeline of 1.6 lakh hotel rooms to open in next five years.
“In recent years, leisure destinations, particularly emerging markets with limited supply and demand from destination weddings, (had) risen sharply in the national rankings. In 2025-26, however, Delhi and Mumbai emerged as the country’s leading RevPAR markets.… Leisure destinations such as Ranthambore, Rishikesh and Udaipur nevertheless remained among the top performers,” said the report.
“The gap at the top also narrowed considerably, with less than Rs 250 separating the four leading markets, compared with a much wider spread in the previous year. Strong performance in these leisure destinations has attracted additional mid-market and upper midmarket supply, resulting in some normalisation in market-wide rates without displacing them from the country’s leading RevPAR markets,” it added.
At the end of March 2026, India had a pipeline of 1.6 lakh hotel rooms to open in next five years. This was a 41% jump from the pipeline of 1.1 lakh exactly a year ago. “The pipeline is now approaching the scale of the country’s existing branded inventory. If it materialises in full, India’s branded hotel inventory would increase by 77% to approximately 3.7 lakh rooms. The top five markets are likely to be relatively unchanged with one exception; Jaipur is likely to surpass Chennai to become the fifth largest market in the country by operating inventory,” it said.

The allegedly exposed dataset is said to contain customers’ personal information, residential…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: An unidentified hacker group operating under the name ‘Siriusim’ has claimed to have obtained confidential customer information allegedly linked to State Bank of India, including personal details, loan applications and account-opening documents.
The claim was highlighted by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse56 in a post on social media platform X. According to the account, the group purportedly possesses about 3.8 lakh data entries in CSV format and 2,722 pdf documents associated with the country’s largest public sector lender.
The allegedly exposed dataset is said to contain customers’ personal information, residential addresses, loan applications, supporting documents and other applicationrelated records. CyberPulse56 first reported the claim on Oct 16, stating that Siriusim had presented the material as its first disclosure of the dataset.
However, the authenticity and origin of the alleged data exposure remain unverified. The reported number of entries also does not establish how many individual customers may have been affected, as multiple records could potentially relate to the same person. There has been no independent confirmation that SBI’s systems were compromised or that the documents originated directly from the bank. CyberPulse56 warned that if the dataset proves genuine, the information could potentially be exploited for 
identity theft
, financial fraud, targeted phishing attacks and fraudulent loan applications.
The allegation comes amid broader concerns over cybersecurity risks facing India’s financial sector. Meanwhile, earlier this year, RBI stepped up cybersecurity requirements for commercial banks.

briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India’s smartphone data entries hone market suffered its steepest contraction in several quarters, with shipments plunging 26% in July–Sept as higher prices put buyers off upgrades and prompted manufacturers to curb supplies ahead of the festive season.
Shipments fell to 35.8 million units, the lowest third-quarter volume since 2016, according to Omdia. The slump also changed the pecking order: Samsung displaced Vivo at the top, while Chinese brands’ combined share slipped to about 68% from 75% a year earlier.
Samsung shipped 6.7 million phones to regain leadership for the first time since early 2024. Its affordable Galaxy A-series supported volumes, while cashback, exchanges and longer financing plans helped attract buyers across price brackets.
Vivo’s shipments dropped 34% to 6.4 million — the sharpest decline among the top five. Repeated price increases disrupted retailers’ inventory planning, while limited supplies of entry-level phones weakened its position. Xiaomi’s traditional appeal of offering more features for the money also came under pressure.
Xiaomi’s traditional appeal of offering more features for the money also came under pressure. 
Rising component costs forced trade-offs on pricing and memory configurations, with shipments falling 28% to 4.7 million. 
OPPO ranked third with 4.9 million units, down 24%. Apple took fifth place with 3.9 million phones. Demand for the iPhone 16 and base iPhone 17, along with stocking ahead of anticipated price increases, supported shipments.
“Fewer exclusive launches, limited affordable SKUs and narrowing promotional differences reduced the online channel’s traditional festive advantage,” said Omdia principal analyst Sanyam Chaurasia.
A later Diwali exaggerated the quarterly fall by shifting some offline festive stocking into Oct. The figures track supplies to sellers, rather than purchases by consumers. But, the weakness could persist beyond the festive calendar.
Omdia expects another low-single-digit decline in 2027, with pricing pressure lasting through at least first half as consumers hold on to phones longer.

With 1,076 deals, it has already reached $32.7 billion during the nine-month period (Jan-Sept, 2026). It was primarily driven by record PEVC investments in Sept 2026 at $6 billion. The PE-VC investments do not include those related to the…
briefs.bodyText:
CHENNAI: Despite ongoing geopolitical disruptions, India’s private equity and venture capital (PE-VC) continues to rise. It is expected to exceed last year’s levels of $39 billion, signalling a consecutive YoY revival. International PE investors’ growing interest in Indian firms is putting greater focus on hard-asset businesses such as infrastructure and domestic manufacturing.
Data sourced by TOI from research firm Venture Intelligence shows that investments to the tune of $39 billion, comprising 1,434 deals, were recorded in CY2025. With 1,076 deals, it has already reached $32.7 billion during the nine-month period (Jan-Sept, 2026). It was primarily driven by record PEVC investments in Sept 2026 at $6 billion. The PE-VC investments do not include those related to the real estate sector.
PEs Double Down On Infrastructure Allocation
“Based on the very strong Jul-Sept quarter investment figures, the PE-VC investment tally for 2026 can be expected to end the year at an amount similar to or higher than the previous year,” Arun Natarajan, founder of Venture Intelligence, said.
After a plunge in PE-VC investments, which dropped to $48.9 billion in CY2022 from $64.4 billion in CY2021, it further decreased to $33.8 billion and $33.5 billion during CY2023 and CY2024, respectively. 
However, it revived last year (CY2025).
Noting that the 
Indian economy
 has been able to withstand many external shocks, including an oil-price-impacting US-Iran war, he said the IPO market has also held up—despite volatility in the secondary markets. “One of the key highlights this year is PE investors doubling down on their infrastructure investments. Large foreign investors have made several mega bets on infrastructure companies across sectors like renewable energy, telecom towers & data centers and toll roads; especially dominant has been the role of Canadian investors—like La Caisse (formerly CDPQ), CPP Investments and Brookfield—who have deployed over $3 billion in infrastructure companies in 2026,” he added.
Aniket Dharamshi, co-founder and managing partner, ValueQuest Investment Advisors, said headline investment numbers in 2026 could exceed last year’s levels, particularly if large infrastructure transactions sustain the momentum seen in the third quarter. “While India offers global investors an opportunity to diversify across sectors and growth drivers, beyond the concentration of capital in a few global technology themes, whether this translates into a higher deployment on core PE-VC will depend on economic and earnings growth, valuation expectations and a more stable investment environment,” he said.
Geopolitics, national security, import substitution and supply-chain resilience are bringing greater strategic importance to businesses with tangible assets and domestic manufacturing capabilities. “At the same time, the AI build-out is creating demand from data centre infrastructure to power. Together, these forces are influencing where private capital is being deployed,” he added.

briefs.headline: Asean emerges as fastest growing region for exports
briefs.deck: Latest data available with the commerce department showed that India’s exports to Asean went up 56% during the first five months of the fiscal year as oil product shipments soared 2.4 times to over $6.1 billion, with Singapore accounting for almost threefourths of it. What also helped was a 20-fold jump in computer hardware to $1.4 billion to Asean countries and strong growth of electric…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: It all boils down to one commodity: Oil products. Asean has emerged as the fastest growing region for India’s exports due to a spurt in petro product shipments – mainly to Singapore -- while the European Union saw the slowest pace of increase during AprilAug as export of petroleum products fell.
Latest data available with the commerce department showed that India’s exports to Asean went up 56% during the first five months of the fiscal year as oil product shipments soared 2.4 times to over $6.1 billion, with Singapore accounting for almost threefourths of it. What also helped was a 20-fold jump in computer hardware to $1.4 billion to Asean countries and strong growth of electric machinery (82% to $1.6 billion) and buffalo meat (42% to $1 billion)
Since March, countries have recalibrated their energy purchases due to the disruption in West Asia.
European Union Sees Slowest Pace Of Increase In April-Aug
In contrast, when it comes to EU, oil product exports fell 21% to $4.6 billion as the Netherlands cut back on purchases from India. While the Netherlands was the top destination for Indian fuel, with exports of $5.3 billion during April-Aug 2025, it has now slipped to the third place, behind Singapore and Tanzania, as the value of shipments crashed 47% to $2.8 billion.
A part of the impact in EU was offset by Spain and Italy. In April-Aug, India’s exports to Spain rose 54% to $3.5 billion, with oil products jumping to $1.1 billion during the period, as against $172 million ayear ago – an over six-fold increase. 
In case of Italy, the jump was even more dramatic as petroleum product exports rose from $4 million during April-Aug 2025 to $659 million so far this year.
Oil exports to North America fell 7% to $1.9 billion and the 8% rise in overall exports to the region, largely the US, was led by iPhones as telecom instruments rose 29% to over $11 billion, accounting for 23.5% of the exports to the region. Pharma exports too fell 5% to just under $4 billion.
Exports to the region slowed as the value of shipments to the US was up just over 6% to $42.8 billion, data showed.

briefs.headline: Garment exports have the potential to grow 25% next year: ITF
briefs.bodyText:
Indian garment exports have the potential for a 25% increase next year and will better performance in the three major markets - USA, UK, and the European Union.
Prabhu Dhamodharan, convenor of the Indian Texpreneurs Federation (ITF), said in a press release that garment exporters are exploring new opportunities under the India–UK trade agreement, including setting up offices and design studios in London. Encouraging buyer responses will translate into higher orders from January. With regard to the European Union, implementation of the India–EU trade agreement next financial year will drive double-digit apparel export growth.
In the American market, with tariff concerns easing, India has an opportunity to regain the recently lost 2% market share within the coming quarter. A limited India–U.S. trade agreement, if finalised, will eventually help raise India’s traditional market share from 6% to 8%.
“With greater stability expected across these three major markets, we anticipate India’s monthly apparel exports rising from $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion in 2027 — a 25% increase. Indian exporters are simultaneously strengthening global competitiveness through technology, automation, and productivity improvements, positioning the industry for renewed export growth,” he said.
Total purchase of readymade garments by the U.S. declined 7.42% to $ 49.1 billion during January–August 2026. However, August recorded marginal growth of 0.46%, indicating early signs of market recovery. India’s apparel exports to the U.S. fell sharply by 26.4% to $ 2.7 billion, compared with 29.4% decline for China, 4.4% for Bangladesh and 0.8% for Vietnam. However, Cambodia grew 6.9% and Indonesia 2.6%, reflecting intense competition.
India’s traditional 6% U.S. market share dropped to 4% in August. Uncertainty over additional U.S. tariffs linked to Russian oil purchases had delayed orders from American buyers. Despite relatively stable volumes in other markets, India’s overall apparel exports declined around 7% during the first half of the current financial year. The recent indication that additional Russia-related tariffs will not be imposed for now has improved confidence among Indian exporters, he added.

stories.deck: India’s Ayush Verma won the gold medal in the men’s shot put F53 event at the Asian Para Games on Wednesday. Ayush’s best throw of 8.16m came in his fifth attempt and helped him finish first in the event.
stories.bodyText:
India’s Ayush Verma won the gold medal in the men’s shot put F53 event at the Asian Para Games on Wednesday.
Ayush’s best throw of 8.16m came in his fifth attempt and helped him finish first in the event.
Iran’s Alireza Hemami won the silver medal with a throw of 8.09m. Kazakhstan’s Makhambet Serikkaliyev took bronze with 6.81m.
Second medal for Ayush
Ayush added a second medal to his tally at the Games. He had won bronze in the men’s javelin throw F53/F54 event on Tuesday.
What is the F53 category?
The F53 category is for athletes who have limited movement in their trunk and legs, while their hand grip is less affected.
Athletes compete from a seated position and use their chest, upper back and shoulders to generate force for their throws.

stories.headline: Asian Para Games: Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag win silver
stories.deck: India’s Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag won the silver medal in the women’s compound doubles event at the Asian Para Games on Wednesday. The 19-year-old Indian pair lost 141-150 to China’s Xu Xueqing and Zhao Jing in the final.
stories.bodyText:
India’s 
Sheetal Devi
 and Payal Nag won the silver medal in the women’s compound doubles event at the Asian Para Games on Wednesday. The Indian pair lost 141-150 to China’s Xu Xueqing and Zhao Jing in the final.
The 19-year-old Indians found it difficult to match their opponents after the opening end and spent the rest of the match trying to catch up.
Sheetal shoots four 10s, Payal struggles
Paris Paralympics bronze medallist Sheetal was more consistent, hitting four 10s during the final. However, Asian Para Games debutant Payal could not match her accuracy. She scored mostly 9s and 8s before hitting a 7 with her final arrow.
Sheetal was born without arms, while Payal is a quadruple amputee. Despite the defeat, the pair finished with a silver medal.
Sheetal wins second successive silver
This was Sheetal’s second consecutive silver medal in the women’s compound doubles event at the Asian Para Games. She had finished second in the previous edition while partnering Sarita Devi.
Sheetal, who is from Loidhar village in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kishtwar district, was born with phocomelia, a rare condition that left her arms severely underdeveloped.
She is also in contention for a gold medal in the individual event.
Payal’s journey to the top
Payal, who is from Odisha, lost all four limbs after coming into contact with an 11,000-volt high-tension power line at the age of eight.
She came into the spotlight in April this year when she beat Sheetal on her way to winning gold at the World Archery Para Series in Bangkok.
Indian men miss bronze by one point
India’s Toman Kumar and Shyam Sunder Swami narrowly missed out on a medal in the men’s compound doubles event. They lost 153-154 to China’s Ai Xinliang and Zhang Yicheng in the bronze-medal match.
Kumar has a permanent physical impairment following the amputation of his left leg. Swami has a locomotor impairment that affects the movement of his lower limbs.

stories.headline: Cricket: Bavuma battles adversity to put South Africa in control
stories.deck: The captain produced a defiant display and showcased his ​batting skills as South Africa recovered from a precarious 110-6 in ⁠the morning session on the third day to declare on 425-9 before taking an Australian wicket prior to stumps, an emphatic response to their heavy defeat in last week’s first ‌test
stories.bodyText:
South Africa captain Temba Bavuma said he enjoyed battling against adversity as he scored 179 on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) to turn around his side’s fortunes in the second test against Australia and also quell some of his own mental demons.
The captain produced a defiant display and showcased his batting skills as South Africa recovered from a precarious 110-6 in the morning session on the third day to declare on 425-9 before taking an Australian wicket prior to stumps, an emphatic response to their heavy defeat in last week’s first test.
The 36-year-old Bavuma had been forced to the crease with the hosts on 12-2 on Sunday’s rain-restricted opening day, when only an hour's play was possible, and had to resume his innings on Monday as the ball moved around after the wet weather finally relented. South Africa slumped to 97-5 by the close of the second day.
“I walked into a tricky situation,” he told reporters. “I think everything was in the bowlers’ favour: the conditions overhead, the wicket itself. We’d just lost two early wickets, but ordinarily I’ve found myself in those situations quite many times and I guess it seems to bring out the best in me."
The sun appeared on Tuesday after two rain-affected days, and the pitch flattened out, offering the batters considerably more assistance, although Bavuma insisted conditions were not as easy as they might have seemed.
Dealing with Austrailia’s quality attack
“With the quality of the bowling attack, they're still able to put you under pressure, even when the ball is slightly softer and older.
“I think from a mindset point of view, for me, nothing really changed. I was always just trying to be as tight as I could and try to hit the ball as straight as I could.
“The one thing was being able to get the team out of a tough situation. But then from a personal point of view, to go on to getting a big 100, that's obviously something that's been a thorn in my side throughout my career. So it was nice to get over that mental hurdle,” he added.
Bavuma, who has overcome a long-standing elbow injury, not only surpassed his previous highest test score but featured in two record partnerships.
He added 132 with Marco Jansen, who scored 85, to set a South African seventh-wicket record at St George’s Park, before putting on a national-record 183 for the eighth wicket with number nine Simon Harmer, who made a test career-best 82.
“They put a heavy price on their wickets and part of our plan was to keep Australia in the field for as long as we could. It all went according to plan,” Bavuma added as Australia will resume at 3–1 at the start of day four.

stories.headline: Harmanpreet Kaur rediscovers her mojo as India sweep series
stories.bodyText:
Former captain Harmanpreet Kaur struggled to keep her emotions in check after a sizzling 91 not out off 41 balls, setting up India's commanding 92-run win over Zimbabwe in the third and final T20I in Raipur on Tuesday (October 20, 2026).
Shafali Verma made an entertaining 69 off 37 balls before Harmanpreet returned to her destructive best to power India 216 for seven.
On expected lines, Zimbabwe could not get anywhere near the massive target and and ended at 124 for seven in 20 overs, with India taking the series 3-0.
The two teams will now head to Vadodara for a three-match ODI series starting on October 23.
The game marked the return to form for Harmanpreet, who was struggling for runs of late and stepped down as captain ahead of the Zimbabwe series.
When in full swing, Harmanpreet enables India to maintain a high-scoring tempo in the middle overs. And that is what happened on Tuesday as she went hammer and tongs following Shafali's fireworks at the top of the order.
Even though it came against a lower-ranked team, the knock would provide Harmanpreet much-needed confidence ahead of the important assignments, including the inaugural six-team ICC Women's Champions Trophy in the shortest format at home early next year.
Not many strike the ball as well as Harmanpreet does and that is what she exhibited in her statement innings.
Captain Smriti Mandhana opted to bat with an aim to give more batters time in the middle.
For that very purpose, she made way for Anushka Sharma (28 off 20) to open the batting alongside Shafali, who scored a second consecutive half-century to lead India's charge.
Anushka and Shafali shared a 54-run stand off 32 balls to set the tone for the innings.
Anushka pulled Tendai Makusha for a thundering six in the fifth over. Shafali, at the other end, hit sixes for fun in her sizzling effort and the majority of her five strikes went over deep mid-wicket.
The Indian opener also effectively employed the sweep against the spinners.
Following Shafali's departure, Harmanpreet extended India's six-hitting spree with five maximums. It was a good surface to bat on, ideal for Harmanpreet to return to her explosive ways.
The 37-year-old had not found her groove on the slow pitches of the Women's T20 Asia Cup and did not get a lot of batting time in the team's triumphant Asian Games campaign in Japan.
"Feels great that I got some time in the middle. Just wanted to enjoy myself and bat as long as possible," said Harmanpreet before breaking down in the middle of the interview during the innings break.
India smashed 62 runs in the last five overs with the loss of four wickets.

briefs.headline: Ramesh Powar appointed as national selector; Ojha to continue as panel chairman
briefs.deck: The BCCI said interim head Ojha will chair the committee based on seniority. The former left-arm spinner played 24 Tests across his five-year-long career
briefs.bodyText:
Former Indian spinner Ramesh Powar was on Monday (October 19, 2026) drafted into the national men's senior selection committee, while Pragyan Ojha remained the chairman of the panel, succeeding Ajit Agarkar, whose term ended on October 4.
The BCCI said interim head Ojha will chair the committee based on seniority. The former left-arm spinner played 24 Tests across his five-year-long career.
"The Cricket Advisory Committee (CAC), comprising former India batters Ashok Malhotra and Jatin Paranjape, unanimously recommended the appointment of Powar," said BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia in a release.
The 48-year-old Powar represented India in two Tests and 31 ODIs during his playing career.
He has since held coaching roles, including head coach of the Indian women's team, Mumbai and Gujarat, besides being a bowling coach at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here.
During his stint with the India Women’s team, Powar marshalled its Asia Cup title win in 2022, and a Commonwealth Games silver medal.
Though his international career was a brief one, Powar, a capable off-spinner, remained a Mumbai stalwart, plucking 470 wickets across 148 first-class matches.
He was also a handy lower-order batter, scoring 4245 runs with seven hundreds and 17 fifties.
PTI understands that the screening process for the new selector was held on October 15 at the BCCI headquarters in Mumbai.
Apart from Powar, former Indian cricketers Salil Ankola, Wasim Jaffer, Jacob Martin and Connor Williams also appeared for the interview.
However, the CAC members zeroed in on Powar to ensure continuity at the helm at least until the 2027 50-over World Cup in South Africa.
Jaffer had played 31 Tests for India between 2000 and 2008, scoring 1944 runs at an average of 34 with five hundreds.
So, had the Mumbaikar been chosen, then he would have replaced Ojha as the chairman of selectors.
The BCCI also lauded Agarkar for rendering remarkable service to Indian cricket as the chairman of selectors.
"The BCCI places on record its appreciation for Mr Ajit Agarkar for his commitment, conviction and contribution during his tenure as Chairman of the Men’s Selection Committee.
"Since his appointment in July 2023, Agarkar led the committee through a significant period for Indian cricket, with India winning three ICC trophies, two Asia Cup titles and back-to-back Asian Games gold medals," Saikia added.
Men's Selection Committee:
Pragyan Ojha (Chairperson), Shiv Sundar Das, RP Singh, Ajay Ratra, Ramesh Powar.

briefs.headline: India bag 14 medals in para athletics, Nishad third Indian to win two golds in single Para Asiad
briefs.deck: India added five gold, four silver, and five bronze medals on the second day of competition, taking the medal count from para athletics to 20, the second best so far after China's 23 (13 gold, 5 silver, 5 bronze)
briefs.bodyText:
Indian para track and field athletes pocketed 14 medals, including five gold, with Nishad Kumar becoming the third from the country to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games here on Tuesday (October 20, 2026).
India added five gold, four silver, and five bronze medals on the second day of competition, taking the medal count from para athletics to 20, the second best so far after China's 23 (13 gold, 5 silver, 5 bronze).
Nishad clinched the top spot in the men's high jump T47 event to join para-runner Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi as only the third Indian to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games.
He had won a gold in the long jump T47 event on Monday (October 19).
On Tuesday (October 20), Nishad sailed over 2.04m to win the gold and set a new Games record.
Ankur (men's 5000m T11 and 1500m T11) and Sheetal (women's individual compound open and mixed team compound open) had won two gold medals each in the previous edition in Hangzhou, China.
The T47 classification is for athletes with upper limb impairments.
Nishad's right arm was severed by a grass-cutting machine at his family farm in Himachal Pradesh's Amb when he was merely six.
It was Deepthi Jeevanji, who began India's gold rush on the day, as she reasserted her continental supremacy by snaring a second consecutive Asian Para Games gold medal in the women's 400m T20 event after clocking a Games record time of 56.36sec.
The 23-year-old from Telangana, who also holds the Asian record, is a two-time Para World Championships medallist, having won the gold in 2024.
The T20 classification covers athletes with intellectual impairments.
Hailing from a remote village in Telangana's Warangal, Deepthi's parents are small farmers who also worked as labourers in their village. Her talent for running was first discovered by a physical education teacher in her school.
She eventually found support from badminton great Pullela Gopichand, who suggested a test for her intellectual disability.
After she burst into the limelight with her consistent international performances, Deepthi revealed the tremendous role her parents played in supporting her ambitions despite being taunted for backing her by their fellow villagers.
Seasoned sprinter Simran also created a new Games record to clinch her maiden gold medal, while compatriot Tejalben Damor fetched a bronze in the women's 200m T12 competition.
Simran clocked 24.80sec, while Tejalben, making her debut at the continental showpiece, was third at 25.23sec.
T12 classification covers athletes with moderate visual impairment.
The 26-year-old Simran, who won a bronze in 2024 Paralympics, is on a comeback trail with her new guide Shivam after her previous guide Umar Saifi was banned for a doping violation.
Hailing from Burari village in Delhi, Simran was born prematurely with impaired vision which makes it difficult for her to see beyond 10m. She was kept in an incubator for seven months after her pre-term birth.
But through sheer grit and determination, she rose to become a top para athlete of the country.
She was mocked by people during childhood for her vision impairment.
In the men's discus throw combined F51/52/53 event, Pranav Soorma won gold with an Asian record, while Ram Ratan Singh took the silver in a 1-2 finish for the country.
The 32-year-old Soorma, who had won gold in the club throw F51 event in the previous Asian Para Games as well as in the 2024 Paralympics, sent his discus to a distance of 11.66m in his fourth attempt to take the top spot and set a new Asian record.
At the age of 16, Soorma's life changed dramatically when a cement sheet fell on his head, causing a severe spinal cord injury that left him paralysed. Doctors told him he would never walk again, and he spent six months in the hospital.
It took several years for Soorma, from Faridabad, to accept that a wheelchair would be his lifelong companion. To maintain a positive mindset, Soorma began meditating. While in the hospital, friends introduced him to para sports, igniting a new passion.
Despite being confined to a wheelchair, Soorma excelled academically, scoring 91.2% in his 12th board exams and pursuing a postgraduate degree in commerce from the prestigious Delhi School of Economics. He later secured a job as an Assistant Manager in a bank.
A former cricketer, Soorma experimented with different para sports and even participated in the Mr. Wheelchair India event.
Indians swept all three medals on offer in the men's discus throw F44/64 event with Devender Kumar winning gold in a four-athlete field.
The 32-year-old Devender took the gold with a throw of 49.71m, while Rakesh and Pardeep Kumar took the silver and bronze respectively.
Devender was born at Kishkandha village in Charkhi Dadri of Haryana. At the age of 21, he and his mother met with a major accident and Devender broke his left leg. His left hip was operated on due to multiple fractures. He was in the hospital for the next two months.
The F44 and F64 represent classifications for athletes with lower limb impairments. The F44 athletes compete without a prosthesis while F64 athletes compete with a prosthesis.
Preeti Pal won a silver in the women's 200m T35 event. Praveen Sharma (men's shot put F11), Ayush Verma (men's javelin F53/54), and Hokato Hotozhe Sema (men's shot put F56/57) won bronze medals.

briefs.headline: Maddison's dream return helps Spurs to long-awaited Premier League win
briefs.deck: Spurs had lost three and drawn three coming into the match and there was a real worry that the London club might face a relegation battle like last season, when it escaped on the final day
briefs.bodyText:
Tottenham beat Coventry City 3-1 at home for its first win of the season and climbed off the bottom of the Premier League table on Friday (October 23).
James Maddison's sublime strike against his boyhood club 14 minutes into the game put Spurs in the driving seat. Coventry equalised early in the second half but Omar Marmoush's curling shot put the home side ahead again and Ben Davies sealed all three points in stoppage time.
Spurs had lost three and drawn three coming into the match and there was a real worry that the London club might face a relegation battle like last season, when it escaped on the final day.
This long-awaited win will not allay those fears but the grit involved against a plucky Coventry will give Spurs fans hope the season can now kick on.
Maddison missed all of last season with an anterior cruciate ligament injury and his return for a first start in 536 days was key, the former Coventry player sending a curving strike into the top corner early on.
“I can't really describe the feeling when the ball hit the net," he said. “Those are the ones that are a bit blurry. They are the ones you dream of during those dark days with the ACL.
“I just wanted to show my quality and show what the team's missed in the last 18 months since my last start.”
The goal put Spurs in the driving seat but their inability to add to the tally looked like it might haunt them after Jack Rudoni drew Coventry level four minutes into the second half.
Goalkeeper Antonín Kinský got a hand on his close-range shot but could not stop it squirming into the net.
However, Marmoush's lovely strike — his first Spurs goal since signing from Manchester City in the summer — calmed nerves at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and Davies' low drive in the sixth minute of injury time relieved all tension in north London.
Spurs rose four places to 16th. Coventry was one place behind.
“I'm very disappointed," Coventry boss Frank Lampard said. “I thought we were really good in our performance, which is hard to say after a 3-1 defeat. The third goal is a mistake, but it distorts the picture of the game. The players showed a belief and we were a threat until the end.”
